། ༈མདོར་བསྟན་པ། དང་པོ། དེ་ལྟ་བས་ན་སོགས་ཚིགས་བཅད་གཅིག་སྟེ། ལམ་ཚོལ་བ་ལ་བདུད་ཀྱི་ལས་མང་དུ་འབྱུང་བ་དེ༷་ལྟ༷་བས༷་ན༷་དེ་བཟློག་པའི་ཕྱིར་ཕྱི་དང་ནང་གི་ཡོངས་སུ་འཛིན་པ་བརྟེན་པར་བྱའོ། །དེ་ཅི་ལྟ་བུ་ཞེ་ན་གང་གིས་བརྟེན་པ་པོ་ནི་བྱང༷་ཆུབ༷་དམ༷་པ༷་ཚོལ༷་བ༷་ཡི༷་བས༷མ་པ༷་དྲག༷་པོ་དང་ལྡན༷་ལ་དེ་བསྒྲུབ་པའི་ཐབས་ལ་མཁས༷་པ་དང་ལྡན་པས༷་སོ། །ཇི་ལྟར་བརྟེན་ན་རང་གི་རྒྱུད་ཀྱི་ང༷་རྒྱ༷ལ༷་ངེས༷་པར་བཅོ༷མ་སྟེ༷་དགེ་བའི་བཤེས་གཉེན་གཞན་ལ་གུས་པ་ཆེན་པོས་ཇི་ལྟར་ནད༷་པའི༷་ཚོགས༷་ཀྱིས༷་རང་གི་ནད་གསོ༷་བའི་ཕྱིར༷་གཞན་སྨན༷་པ༷་བཟང་པོ་ལ་བསྟེན༷་པ༷་ལྟར༷་ཆོས་ཉན་པའི་སྐབས་སུའང་། རང་ལ་ནད་པ་ཆོས་སྨྲ་བ་ལ་སྨན་པ་ཆོས་ལ་སྨན་ནན་ཏན་ཉམས་སུ་ལེན་པ་ལ་ནད་གསོ་བའི་འདུ་ཤེས་བཞི་དང་ལྡན་པས་གཡེལ༷་བ༷་མེ༷ད་པར༷་བསྟེན་པར་བྱའོ། །གང་བསྟེན་ན་དགེ༷་བའི༷་བཤེས༷་གཉེན༷་ཏེ་དགེ་བ་ནི་སྐབས་འདིར་ཐེག་པ་ཆེན་པོའི་ཆོས་ཡིན་ལ། དེ་ལེགས་པར་སྟོན་པ་ནི་དགེ་བའི་བཤེས་གཉེན་ཡིན་ཏེ། ལམ་ཡང་དག་པར་སྟོན་པ་དང་ལམ་གྱི་བར་ཆད་བདུད་ཀྱི་ལས་ངོས་ཟིན་པར་བྱེད་ཅིང་དེ་ལས་འདའ་བའི་ཐབས་སྟོན་པའི་སྒོ་ནས་ལམ་ལས་མི་ཉམས་པ་འདིས་ཡོངས་སུ་འཛིན་ནུས་པའི་ཕྱིར་རོ། །དེས་ན་དེ་ལྟ་བུ་ཡོངས་སུ་བསྟེན༷་པ༷ར་བྱའོ༷།
[1-325] translation already produced for this document:
The brief teaching. First, one verse starting with "Therefore": Since many activities of māra arise for those seeking the path, "therefore", in order to reverse them, one should rely on outer and inner upholders. What are they like? Who relies on them? By one who "possesses" a "strong" "intent" "seeking" "supreme" "awakening", and who possesses "skill" in the methods to accomplish it. How do they rely? Having "definitely" "destroyed" "conceit" in their own mind-stream, with great respect for another, a spiritual friend, "just as" a "multitude" of "sick people" "rely" on another good "physician" "to" "cure" their own illness, even during the occasion of listening to the dharma, possessing the four recognitions of oneself as a sick person, the dharma preacher as a physician, the dharma as medicine, and earnest practice as curing the illness, they should rely on them "without" "slackening". Upon whom do they rely? A "spiritual" "friend". Here, "virtue" (spiritual) is the dharma of the mahāyāna, and the one who teaches it well is a spiritual friend, because they are able to completely uphold one so as not to deteriorate from the path by authentically teaching the path, making one recognize the interruptions to the path, the activities of māra, and teaching the methods to transcend them. Therefore, they should completely "rely" upon such a one.

[1-326] source:
།༈རྒྱས་པར་བཤད་པ། གཉིས་པ་ལ་ཕྱི་ནང་གི་ཡོངས་འཛིན་གཉིས་བཤད་པ་དང་། ནང་གི་ཡོངས་འཛིན་བྱེ་བྲག་ཏུ་བཤད་པ་གཉིས

[1-327] source:
།༈ཕྱི་ནང་གི་ཡོངས་འཛིན་གཉིས་བཤད་པ། དང་པོ། སངས་རྒྱས་བྱང་ཆུབ་སོགས་ཚིགས་བཅད་གཅིག་སྟེ། བསྟེན་པར་བྱ་བའི་བཤེས་གཉེན་དེ་གང་ཞེ་ན་འདི་ལྟ་སྟེ། སངས༷་རྒྱས༷་བཅོམ་ལྡན་འདས་རྣམས་དང་བྱང༷་ཆུབ༷་མཆོག༷་ལ་ཞུགས༷་པའི་བྱང༷་ཆུབ༷་སེམ༷ས་དཔའ༷་དག༷་དང་། ལམ་ཕ༷་རོལ༷་ཏུ་ཕྱིན༷་པ་དང༷་བཅས༷་ཏེ༷་དགེ༷་བའི༷་བཤེས༷་སུ༷་བསྟེན༷་པར་བྱའོ། །དེ་ཡང་སངས་རྒྱས་དང་བྱང་ཆུབ་སེམས་དཔའ་དེ༷་དག༷་ནི་ཐེག་པ་ཆེན་པོ་འདི་གཞན་ལ་རྗེས༷་སུ༷་སྟོན༷་པར་བྱེ༷ད་པ་ཡིན་པས་ཕྱིའི་ཡོངས་འཛིན་ཞེས་བྱ་ལ། དེ་དག་གིས་བསྟན་པ་ལམ་ཕ་རོལ་ཏུ་ཕྱིན་པ་འདི༷་ནི༷་ཉམས་སུ་ལེན་པའམ་བསྒྲུབ༷་པར་བྱ་བའི༷་ས༷འམ་གན༷ས་ཡིན་པས་ནང་གི་ཡོངས་འཛིན་ཞེས་བྱའོ། །དེ་ལྟར་ཕྱི་ནང་གི་ཡོངས་འཛིན་དེས་ཐེག་པ་མཆོག་གི་ལམ་ལས་ལམ་གཞན་དུ་མི་ལྟུང་བར་འཛིན་པས་ན་ཡོངས་འཛིན་གཉིས་པོ་དེ་བསྟེན་པའི་རྒྱུ༷་རྣམ༷་པ་དེ་གཉི༷ས་ཀྱིས༷་སངས༷་རྒྱས༷་ཀྱི་བྱང༷་ཆུབ༷་མྱུར༷་དུ༷་རྟོགས༷་པར་འགྱུར༷་ཏེ་མ་ཚང་བ་མེད་པའི་རྒྱུ་ཕུན་སུམ་ཚོགས་པར་གྱུར་པའི་ཕྱིར་རོ། །༈ནང་གི་ཡོངས་འཛིན་བྱེ་བྲག་ཏུ་བཤད་པ།
[1-327] translation already produced for this document:
Explaining the two, the outer and inner upholders. First, one verse starting with "Buddhas, bodhisattvas": Who is that spiritual friend to be relied upon? It is as follows: One should "rely" on the transcendent conquerors, the "Buddhas", "and" the "bodhisattvas" "engaged" in "supreme" "awakening", "along with" the path of the "perfection", "as" "spiritual" "friends". Moreover, "these" Buddhas and bodhisattvas "teach" this mahāyāna to others, so they are called outer upholders. And "this" path of the perfection, which is taught by them, is the "ground" or state "to be accomplished" or practiced, so it is called the inner upholder. Thus, because those outer and inner upholders uphold one so as not to fall from the path of the supreme vehicle to other paths, "by" "those" "two" "types" of "causes"—relying on those two upholders—one "will" "swiftly" "realize" the "awakening" of a "Buddha", because the excellent causes have been gathered without anything missing. Explaining the inner upholder in particular.

། ༈ཤེར་ཕྱིན་བཤེས་གཉེན་ཡིན་ཚུལ། དང་པོ། རྒྱལ་བ་འདས་དང་སོགས་ཚིགས་བཅད་གཅིག་སྟེ། གང་སངས་རྒྱས་དང་བྱང་ཆུབ་སེམས་དཔའ་རྣམས་ནི་དགེ་བའི་བཤེས་གཉེན་ཡིན་པར་ཡོངས་སུ་གྲགས་མོད་ཀྱི། ཤེས་རབ་ཀྱི་ཕ་རོལ་ཏུ་ཕྱིན་པ་དགེ་བའི་བཤེས་གཉེན་དུ་གྱུར་པའི་ཚུལ་ཇི་ལྟར་ཡིན་སྙམ་ན། རྒྱལ༷་བ༷་རྫོགས་པའི་སངས་རྒྱས་གང་ཞིག་སྔར་འདས༷་པའི་དུས་སུ་བྱོན་ཟིན་པ་དང༷་། ད་ལྟ་མ༷་བྱོན༷་པ་མ་འོངས་པའི་སངས་རྒྱས་དང་། ད་ལྟ་སངས་རྒྱས་ནས་ཕྱོགས༷་བཅུར༷་གང༷་བཞུགས༷་པ༷་སྟེ་དུས་གསུམ་གྱི་རྒྱལ་བ་དེ་དག་ཀུན༷་གྱི་ལམ༷་ནི་ཤེས་རབ་ཀྱི་ཕ༷་རོལ༷་ཏུ་ཕྱིན༷་པ༷་འདི༷་ཉིད་ཡི༷ན་གྱི་འདི་ལས་གཞན༷་ནི་མ༷་ཡི༷ན་ཏེ། ཤེས་རབ་ཀྱི་ཕ་རོལ་ཏུ་ཕྱིན་པ་ལ་མ་བརྟེན་པར་འཚང་རྒྱ་བའི་ལམ་གཞན་ནི་རྣམ་པ་ཀུན་ཏུ་མི་སྲིད་དེ་སྲིད་ཞི་མཉམ་ཉིད་དུ་རྟོགས་པའི་ཤེས་རབ་མེད་པའི་ལམ་གཞན་གྱིས་འཚང་རྒྱ་མི་ནུས་པར་ངེས་པའི་ཕྱིར་རོ། །ཤེས་རབ་ཀྱི་ཕ༷་རོལ༷་ཏུ་ཕྱིན༷་པ་འདི༷་ནི་བྱང༷་ཆུབ༷་མཆོག༷་གི་ཚུལ་ལ༷་ཞུགས༷་པ་རྣམ༷ས་ཀྱི༷་གསལ༷་བྱེད་དུ་གྱུར་པ་དང༷་སྒྲོན༷་མར་གྱུར་པ་དང༷་སྣང༷་བར་གྱུར་པ་དང༷་སྟོན༷་པ་མཆོ༷ག་ཏུ་གྱུར་པ་ཡི༷ན་ནོ་ཞེས༷་སུ་རྒྱལ་བ་རྣམས་ཀྱིས་བཤ༷ད་དེ། རིམ་པ་ལྟར་གང་ཟག་གི་བདག་མེད་པ་སྟོན་པ་དང་། ཆོས་ཀྱི་བདག་མེད་པ་སྟོན་པ་དང་། འཇིག་རྟེན་དང་འཇིག་རྟེན་ལས་འདས་པའི་ཆོས་ཐམས་ཅད་སྟོན་པ་དང་། མཐར་ཐུག་གི་འབྲས་བུ་རྣམ་པ་ཐམས་ཅད་མཁྱེན་པའི་བྱང་ཆུབ་ཀྱི་ལམ་སྟོན་པའི་ཕྱིར་ནའོ། །༈བཤེས་གཉེན་དེ་ཇི་ལྟར་བསྟེན་ཚུལ།
[1-329] translation already produced for this document:
How the perfection of wisdom is a spiritual friend. First, one verse starting with "Conquerors of the past": While it is widely renowned that buddhas and bodhisattvas are spiritual friends, one might wonder how the perfection of wisdom becomes a spiritual friend. The "conquerors", the perfect buddhas who "have" already appeared "in the past", "and" the future buddhas who have "not" yet "come", and those who have awakened and "who" "abide" "in the ten directions" right now—the "path" "of all" those conquerors of the three times "is" "this" very "perfection" "of" "wisdom", and it "is" "not" "other" than this. It is completely impossible for there to be another path to awakening without relying on the perfection of wisdom, because it is certain that one cannot awaken through another path lacking the wisdom that realizes the equality of existence and peace. The conquerors "have stated" "that" "this" "perfection" "of wisdom" "is" what becomes the "illuminator", "and" becomes the "lamp", "and" becomes the "light", "and" becomes the "supreme" "teacher" "of those" "engaged" "in" the manner of "supreme" "awakening". This is because it teaches, respectively, the selflessness of persons, the selflessness of phenomena, all worldly and transcendent phenomena, and the path of the ultimate result, the awakening of omniscience. How to rely on that spiritual friend.

[1-332] source:
དང་པོ་ཇི་ལྟར་ཤེས་རབ་སོགས་ཚིགས་བཅད་གཅིག་སྟེ། འཕགས་པ་བརྒྱད་སྟོང་པར་ཤེར་ཕྱིན་གྱི་མཚན་ཉིད་ཞུས་པའི་ལན་དུ། ཤེས་རབ་ཀྱི་ཕ་རོལ་ཏུ་ཕྱིན་པ་ནི་སྟོང་པ་ཉིད་ཀྱི་མཚན་ཉིད་དོ་ཞེས་ཐ་སྙད་ཀྱི་མཚན་ཉིད་མ་བསྟན་པར་དོན་དམ་པའི་མཚན་ཉིད་བསྟན་ཏེ་གཟུགས་སུ་རུང་བ་གཟུགས་ཀྱི་མཚན་ཉིད་ལ་སོགས་པ་ཐ་སྙད་ཀྱི་གནས་ཚུལ་ནི་དོན་དམ་དུ་མ་གྲུབ་པར་བློས་བཏགས་པ་ཙམ་སྟེ་དཔྱད་མི་བཟོད་པའོ། །ཆོས་ཀུན་གྱི་གནས་ཚུལ་རྣལ་མ་ནི་སྟོང་པ་ཉིད་དེ། ཡིན་ལུགས་སྐྱོན་མེད་པ་ཡིན་པས་ན་དེ་ལྟར་གསུངས་སོ་འདིར་ཡང་དེ་བཞིན་དུ། ཇི༷་ལྟར༷་ཤེས༷་རབ༷་ཀྱི་ཕ༷་རོལ༷་ཏུ་ཕྱིན༷་པའི༷་མཚ༷ན་ཉི༷ད་ནི་སྟོང༷་པ་ཉིད་ཡིན་ལ། དེ་ཁོ་ནའི་མཚན་ཉིད་སྟོང་པ་ཉིད་ཡིན་པར་མ་ཟད་ཀྱི་གཟུགས་ལ་སོགས་པ་ཆོས༷་འདི༷་ཐམ༷ས་ཅ༷ད་ཀྱི་མཚ༷ན་ཉི༷ད་ཀྱང་ཤེར་ཕྱིན་དེ༷་དང༷་འདྲ༷་བར་སྟོང་པ་ཉིད་དུ་ཤེས༷་ཤིང༷་། ཆོས༷་སུ་གདགས་པ་ཇི་སྙེད་པ་རྣམ༷ས་ཐམས་ཅད་ངོ་བོ་སྟོང༷་ཞིང༷་དམིགས་པའི་མཚ༷ན་མ༷་མེ༷ད་པར༷་རབ༷་ཏུ་ཤེས༷་ན༷། དེ༷་ལྟར༷་སྤྱོ༷ད་པ༷་དེ་ནི་བདེ༷་བར་གཤེ༷གས་པའི་ཤེས༷་རབ༷་ཀྱི་ཕར་ཕྱིན་ལ་སྤྱོ༷ད་པ༷་ཡི༷ན་ནོ། །
[1-332] translation already produced for this document:
First, one verse starting with "Just as the wisdom": In the Noble Eight Thousand-Line Prajñāpāramitā, in response to a question about the defining characteristic of the perfection of wisdom, it states, "The perfection of wisdom is characterized by emptiness," thus teaching the ultimate characteristic without teaching the conventional characteristic; for conventional modes of abiding, such as form being characterized by suitability as form, are not established ultimately, but are merely imputed by the mind and cannot withstand analysis. The genuine mode of abiding of all phenomena is emptiness, and since this is the flawless natural state, it was taught as such. Here, too, in the same way, "just as" the "characteristic" "of" the "perfection" "of" "wisdom" is emptiness, not only is the characteristic of that alone emptiness, but one also "knows" the "characteristic" of "all" "these" "phenomena", such as form, to be emptiness, "similar" "to" "that" perfection of wisdom, "and" "if" one "thoroughly" "knows" that "all" designated "phenomena" whatsoever are empty in essence "and" "without" "marks" of apprehension, "that" "practice" "in" "that" "manner" "is" "practicing" the "perfection" "of" "wisdom" of the "sugatas".

[1-333] source:

Second, there are three: the actual meaning, its example, and the concluding summary of what was taught in that manner.

heading: **དེ་ལྟར་བསྟན་པའི་མཇུག་བསྡུ་བ།**
translation: Third, one verse starting with "Just as it is apprehended": "Just" "as" one "apprehends" self and what belongs to self to exist even though they do not exist in the mode of abiding, it "was" "taught" that "likewise", through the power of one's own conceptuality, one becomes "afflicted". And if one does "not" "apprehend" "self" "and" what belongs to "self" in accordance with the factual mode of abiding, it "was" "stated" that one becomes "purified". Although there is affliction and purification conventionally in that way, in "this" authentic natural state there is "no" person "whatsoever" becoming "afflicted" and that affliction "also" becoming "purified"; rather, the "bodhisattva" "realizes" the "perfection" "of" "wisdom", which is equality from the very beginning. Instruction on the necessity of relying on that perfection of wisdom.

"Likewise", "the" "bodhisattva" who "practices" the "supreme" "perfection" "of" "wisdom", who is like the sun free from the clouds of obscurations, being "learned" in "practicing" "emptiness" "and" "signlessness", thoroughly emits the supreme network of light rays of Dharma; and thereby "having" "destroyed" the "thick" black darkness of "viewing" self and phenomena without exception, they "overpower" "all" firefly-like "beings", "and" other creature-like "arhats", "and" star-like "pratyekabuddhas", "and" "many" moon-like other "bodhisattvas" who are devoid of the skillful means of this perfection of wisdom. Through wisdom, they are distinguished above all other practices that do not possess this.
style_instruction: Translate this passage of a Tibetan Buddhist commentary on the Verse Summary of the Perfection of Wisdom (Ratnaguṇasañcayagāthā) into clear, accurate English prose. Translate the whole passage completely and in the same order: do not summarise, shorten or omit anything, and keep the same number of lines as the source. Where the commentary quotes or glosses words of the root verses, keep those quoted words recognisable in the translation. Keep proper names in their standard Sanskrit forms (Subhūti, Śāriputra, Maitreya, Haribhadra) and technical terms recognisable (prajñāpāramitā = perfection of wisdom, bodhisattva). Do not add commentary, notes, or explanation of your own.

དང་པོ། ཉི་མ་སྤྲིན་དང་སོགས་ཚིགས་བཅད་གཉིས་ཏེ། དཔེར་ན་ཉི༷་མ༷་སྤྲིན༷་དང༷་བྲལ༷་བའི༷་འོ༷ད་ཟེར༷་གྱིས་དྲྭ༷་བ༷་ཅ༷ན་མུན༷་ནག༷་ཐིབས༷་པོ༷་དང་གཞན་ཡང་མུན༷་པ༷་ཐམ༷ས་ཅ༷ད་འཇོམས༷་པ་དེ་འཆར༷་བ༷་ན། རང་གི་ལུས་ཀྱི་ཕྱོགས་གཅིག་ཙམ་ན་འོད་ཕྲ་མོ་ཡོད་པ་སྲིན༷་བུ༷་མེ༷་ཁྱེར༷་དང་། རང་གི་ལུས་ཀྱི་འོད་དང་སྒྲོན་མེ་སོགས་ཐོགས་པའི་མཐུས་ཉེ་སྐོར་ཙམ་སྣང་བར་བྱེད་པ་སྲོག༷་ཆག༷ས་འབྱུང༷་པོ༷་ཐམ༷ས་ཅ༷ད་དང༷་། ཅུང་ཟད་སྣང་བ་སྐར༷་མའི༷་ཚོགས༷་དང༷་། ཕལ་ཆེར་སྣང་བ་ཟླ༷་བའི༷་འོ༷ད་དེ་དེ་ལྟར་འོད་བཞི་པོ་ཀུན༷་ཟིལ༷་གྱིས༷་གནོན༷་པ། དེ༷་བཞིན༷་དུ་བྱང༷་ཆུབ༷་སེམ༷ས་དཔའ༷་ཤེས༷་རབ༷་ཀྱི་ཕ༷་རོལ༷་ཏུ་ཕྱིན༷་པ་མཆོག༷་ལ་སྤྱོ༷ད་པ་སྒྲིབ་པའི་སྤྲིན་དང་བྲལ་བའི་ཉི་མ་ལྟ་བུ་དེ་ནི། སྟོང༷་པ༷་ཉིད་དང༷་ནི༷་མཚ༷ན་མ༷་མེ༷ད་པར་སྤྱོ༷ད་པ༷་ལ་མཁས༷་པས༷་ཆོས་ཀྱི་འོད་ཟེར་མཆོག་གི་དྲྭ་བ་རབ་ཏུ་འགྱེད་པས་བདག་དང་ཆོས་སུ་ལྟ༷་བའི༷་མུན་ནག་ཐིབས༷་པོ༷་མ་ལུས་པ་བཅོ༷མ་ནས༷་མེ་ཁྱེར་ལྟ་བུའི་འགྲོ༷་བ་ཀུན༷་དང༷་། སྲོག་ཆགས་གཞན་ལྟ་བུའི་དགྲ༷་བཅོ༷མ་པ་དང་། སྐར་མ་ལྟ་བུའི་རང༷་རྒྱལ༷་དང་། ཟླ་བ་ལྟ་བུའི་བྱང༷་ཆུབ༷་སེམ༷ས་དཔའ་གཞན་ཤེས་རབ་ཕར་ཕྱིན་འདི་ཡི་ཐབས་མཁས་དང་བྲལ་བ་མང༷་པོ༷་ཟིལ༷་གྱིས༷་གནོན༷་ཏེ། ཤེས་རབ་ཀྱི་སྒོ་ནས་འདི་དང་མི་ལྡན་པའི་བསྒྲུབ་པ་གཞན་ཐམས་ཅད་ལས་ཁྱད་པར་དུ་འཕགས་པའོ།

དང་པོ། ཉི་མ་སྤྲིན་དང་སོགས་ཚིགས་བཅད་གཉིས་ཏེ། དཔེར་ན་ཉི༷་མ༷་སྤྲིན༷་དང༷་བྲལ༷་བའི༷་འོ༷ད་ཟེར༷་གྱིས་དྲྭ༷་བ༷་ཅ༷ན་མུན༷་ནག༷་ཐིབས༷་པོ༷་དང་གཞན་ཡང་མུན༷་པ༷་ཐམ༷ས་ཅ༷ད་འཇོམས༷་པ་དེ་འཆར༷་བ༷་ན། རང་གི་ལུས་ཀྱི་ཕྱོགས་གཅིག་ཙམ་ན་འོད་ཕྲ་མོ་ཡོད་པ་སྲིན༷་བུ༷་མེ༷་ཁྱེར༷་དང་། རང་གི་ལུས་ཀྱི་འོད་དང་སྒྲོན་མེ་སོགས་ཐོགས་པའི་མཐུས་ཉེ་སྐོར་ཙམ་སྣང་བར་བྱེད་པ་སྲོག༷་ཆག༷ས་འབྱུང༷་པོ༷་ཐམ༷ས་ཅ༷ད་དང༷་། ཅུང་ཟད་སྣང་བ་སྐར༷་མའི༷་ཚོགས༷་དང༷་། ཕལ་ཆེར་སྣང་བ་ཟླ༷་བའི༷་འོ༷ད་དེ་དེ་ལྟར་འོད་བཞི་པོ་ཀུན༷་ཟིལ༷་གྱིས༷་གནོན༷་པ། དེ༷་བཞིན༷་དུ་བྱང༷་ཆུབ༷་སེམ༷ས་དཔའ༷་ཤེས༷་རབ༷་ཀྱི་ཕ༷་རོལ༷་ཏུ་ཕྱིན༷་པ་མཆོག༷་ལ་སྤྱོ༷ད་པ་སྒྲིབ་པའི་སྤྲིན་དང་བྲལ་བའི་ཉི་མ་ལྟ་བུ་དེ་ནི། སྟོང༷་པ༷་ཉིད་དང༷་ནི༷་མཚ༷ན་མ༷་མེ༷ད་པར་སྤྱོ༷ད་པ༷་ལ་མཁས༷་པས༷་ཆོས་ཀྱི་འོད་ཟེར་མཆོག་གི་དྲྭ་བ་རབ་ཏུ་འགྱེད་པས་བདག་དང་ཆོས་སུ་ལྟ༷་བའི༷་མུན་ནག་ཐིབས༷་པོ༷་མ་ལུས་པ་བཅོ༷མ་ནས༷་མེ་ཁྱེར་ལྟ་བུའི་འགྲོ༷་བ་ཀུན༷་དང༷་། སྲོག་ཆགས་གཞན་ལྟ་བུའི་དགྲ༷་བཅོ༷མ་པ་དང་། སྐར་མ་ལྟ་བུའི་རང༷་རྒྱལ༷་དང་། ཟླ་བ་ལྟ་བུའི་བྱང༷་ཆུབ༷་སེམ༷ས་དཔའ་གཞན་ཤེས་རབ་ཕར་ཕྱིན་འདི་ཡི་ཐབས་མཁས་དང་བྲལ་བ་མང༷་པོ༷་ཟིལ༷་གྱིས༷་གནོན༷་ཏེ། ཤེས་རབ་ཀྱི་སྒོ་ནས་འདི་དང་མི་ལྡན་པའི་བསྒྲུབ་པ་གཞན་ཐམས་ཅད་ལས་ཁྱད་པར་དུ་འཕགས་པའོ།

དང་པོ། ཉི་མ་སྤྲིན་དང་སོགས་ཚིགས་བཅད་གཉིས་ཏེ། དཔེར་ན་ཉི༷་མ༷་སྤྲིན༷་དང༷་བྲལ༷་བའི༷་འོ༷ད་ཟེར༷་གྱིས་དྲྭ༷་བ༷་ཅ༷ན་མུན༷་ནག༷་ཐིབས༷་པོ༷་དང་གཞན་ཡང་མུན༷་པ༷་ཐམ༷ས་ཅ༷ད་འཇོམས༷་པ་དེ་འཆར༷་བ༷་ན། རང་གི་ལུས་ཀྱི་ཕྱོགས་གཅིག་ཙམ་ན་འོད་ཕྲ་མོ་ཡོད་པ་སྲིན༷་བུ༷་མེ༷་ཁྱེར༷་དང་། རང་གི་ལུས་ཀྱི་འོད་དང་སྒྲོན་མེ་སོགས་ཐོགས་པའི་མཐུས་ཉེ་སྐོར་ཙམ་སྣང་བར་བྱེད་པ་སྲོག༷་ཆག༷ས་འབྱུང༷་པོ༷་ཐམ༷ས་ཅ༷ད་དང༷་། ཅུང་ཟད་སྣང་བ་སྐར༷་མའི༷་ཚོགས༷་དང༷་། ཕལ་ཆེར་སྣང་བ་ཟླ༷་བའི༷་འོ༷ད་དེ་དེ་ལྟར་འོད་བཞི་པོ་ཀུན༷་ཟིལ༷་གྱིས༷་གནོན༷་པ། དེ༷་བཞིན༷་དུ་བྱང༷་ཆུབ༷་སེམ༷ས་དཔའ༷་ཤེས༷་རབ༷་ཀྱི་ཕ༷་རོལ༷་ཏུ་ཕྱིན༷་པ་མཆོག༷་ལ་སྤྱོ༷ད་པ་སྒྲིབ་པའི་སྤྲིན་དང་བྲལ་བའི་ཉི་མ་ལྟ་བུ་དེ་ནི། སྟོང༷་པ༷་ཉིད་དང༷་ནི༷་མཚ༷ན་མ༷་མེ༷ད་པར་སྤྱོ༷ད་པ༷་ལ་མཁས༷་པས༷་ཆོས་ཀྱི་འོད་ཟེར་མཆོག་གི་དྲྭ་བ་རབ་ཏུ་འགྱེད་པས་བདག་དང་ཆོས་སུ་ལྟ༷་བའི༷་མུན་ནག་ཐིབས༷་པོ༷་མ་ལུས་པ་བཅོ༷མ་ནས༷་མེ་ཁྱེར་ལྟ་བུའི་འགྲོ༷་བ་ཀུན༷་དང༷་། སྲོག་ཆགས་གཞན་ལྟ་བུའི་དགྲ༷་བཅོ༷མ་པ་དང་། སྐར་མ་ལྟ་བུའི་རང༷་རྒྱལ༷་དང་། ཟླ་བ་ལྟ་བུའི་བྱང༷་ཆུབ༷་སེམ༷ས་དཔའ་གཞན་ཤེས་རབ་ཕར་ཕྱིན་འདི་ཡི་ཐབས་མཁས་དང་བྲལ་བ་མང༷་པོ༷་ཟིལ༷་གྱིས༷་གནོན༷་ཏེ། ཤེས་རབ་ཀྱི་སྒོ་ནས་འདི་དང་མི་ལྡན་པའི་བསྒྲུབ་པ་གཞན་ཐམས་ཅད་ལས་ཁྱད་པར་དུ་འཕགས་པའོ།

translation: First, two verses starting with "Whenever bodhisattvas": Although māras do not find an opportunity against a bodhisattva who is endowed with skillful means and the armor of wisdom as explained above, they do find an opportunity against those of lesser capacity who are not endowed with that method. Furthermore, the Aṣṭasāhasrikā mentions seven faults by which māras find an opportunity, and the Pañcaviṃśatisāhasrikā mentions twelve; what is taught here is the last of them: "At" "which" "time" "bodhisattvas" "fight" with their bodies "and" "dispute" with their speech with one another, "and", in mutual "disharmony", "become" "endowed" "with" "angry" minds, "at" "that" "time", the sinful "māras" "rejoice", "and" however much the dispute increases, to that extent they "become" "supremely" "joyful"; the reason for that is because they "think": "Due to the fault of that dispute, which contradicts the path of skillful means and wisdom, 'both' of 'those' bodhisattvas 'become' 'distant' 'from' the 'wisdom' 'of' the 'Victorious' 'Ones', and we have found an opportunity." In this way, "both" of "them" "become" "distant" from the wisdom of a Buddha, "and", with untamed mindstreams, they "become" "like" "flesh-eating" demons, such as rākṣasas and pretas. "Both" the one who gets angry and the one who retaliates against anger "will" "violate", through dispute, "their" "own" "vow" to attain perfect awakening out of compassion for the sake of others and to practice its path, the perfections; for disputing with anger contradicts in every way compassion, bodhicitta, the wisdom that sees selflessness, and so forth. For one who "hates" "and" is "devoid" "of" its antidote, "patience", "how" "could" "there" "be" the attainment of "awakening"? It is like a sprout from a burnt seed. "At" "that" "time", when such dispute has occurred, the "māras", "together" "with" those who belong to their "own" "partisan" side, "will" "rejoice", because it has been accomplished according to their intentions. Therefore, it is extensively stated in the sūtras that for a bodhisattva, the arising of anger for even an instant is a greater fault than the arising of the fault of attachment for an eon, because it contradicts compassion in every way; and in particular, anger directed toward the object of a bodhisattva is a great fault. As it is said in the Dharma discourse of the Ratnakūṭa called Maitreyamahāsiṃhanāda: "One should flee a hundred yojanas away from a place with angry disputes; one should not generate an angry mind. Fighting and generating an angry mind toward another bodhisattva is a far heavier fault than scolding, striking, and attacking with weapons all the sentient beings of the great trichiliocosm, and by it a bodhisattva is wounded and degenerates; for example, just as iron is not cut by things other than iron such as clods of earth and so forth, the roots of virtue of a bodhisattva are also exhausted by anger toward another bodhisattva, whereas they cannot be exhausted by other things; therefore, they should treat one another with reverence and respect, and one should generate the perception of the Teacher even toward a bodhisattva who has first generated the mind."

བྱམས་པ་སེང་གེ་སྒྲ་ཆེན་པོ་ཞེས་བྱ་བ་དཀོན་མཆོག་བརྩེགས་པའི་ཆོས་ཀྱི་རྣམ་གྲངས་ལས། ཞེ་སྡང་གི་རྩོད་པ་དང་བཅས་པའི་གནས་ལས་དཔག་ཚད་བརྒྱར་འབྱོལ་བར་བྱ་སྟེ། ཞེ་སྡང་གི་སེམས་བསྐྱེད་པར་མི་བྱའོ། །སྟོང་གསུམ་གྱི་སྟོང་ཆེན་པོའི་འཇིག་རྟེན་ཁམས་ཀྱི་སེམས་ཅན་ཐམས་ཅད་ལ་སྤྱོས་ཤིང་བརྡེག་ལ་མཚོན་གྱིས་བཏབ་པ་བས་བྱང་ཆུབ་སེམས་དཔའ་གཞན་ལ་ཐབ་དང་ཞེ་སྡང་གི་སེམས་བསྐྱེད་པ་དེ་ཆེས་ཉེས་པ་ལྕི་ཞིང་དེས་བྱང་ཆུབ་སེམས་དཔའ་སྨས་པ་དང་ཉམས་པར་འགྱུར་ཏེ། གཅིག་གིས་གཅིག་ལ་ཞེ་ས་དང་གུས་པ་དང་བཅས་པར་བྱ་སྟེ་སེམས་དང་པོ་བསྐྱེད་པའི་བྱང་ཆུབ་སེམས་དཔའ་ལ་ཡང་སྟོན་པའི་འདུ་ཤེས་བསྐྱེད་པར་བྱའོ། །ཞེས་གསུངས་པ་བཞིན་ནོ།

First, two verses starting with "Whenever bodhisattvas": Although māras do not find an opportunity against a bodhisattva who is endowed with skillful means and the armor of wisdom as explained above, they do find an opportunity against those of lesser capacity who are not endowed with that method. Furthermore, the Aṣṭasāhasrikā mentions seven faults by which māras find an opportunity, and the Pañcaviṃśatisāhasrikā mentions twelve; what is taught here is the last of them: "At" "which" "time" "bodhisattvas" "fight" with their bodies "and" "dispute" with their speech with one another, "and", in mutual "disharmony", "become" "endowed" "with" "angry" minds, "at" "that" "time", the sinful "māras" "rejoice", "and" however much the dispute increases, to that extent they "become" "supremely" "joyful"; the reason for that is because they "think": "Due to the fault of that dispute, which contradicts the path of skillful means and wisdom, 'both' of 'those' bodhisattvas 'become' 'distant' 'from' the 'wisdom' 'of' the 'Victorious' 'Ones', and we have found an opportunity." In this way, "both" of "them" "become" "distant" from the wisdom of a Buddha, "and", with untamed mindstreams, they "become" "like" "flesh-eating" demons, such as rākṣasas and pretas. "Both" the one who gets angry and the one who retaliates against anger "will" "violate", through dispute, "their" "own" "vow" to attain perfect awakening out of compassion for the sake of others and to practice its path, the perfections; for disputing with anger contradicts in every way compassion, bodhicitta, the wisdom that sees selflessness, and so forth. For one who "hates" "and" is "devoid" "of" its antidote, "patience", "how" "could" "there" "be" the attainment of "awakening"? It is like a sprout from a burnt seed. "At" "that" "time", when such dispute has occurred, the "māras", "together" "with" those who belong to their "own" "partisan" side, "will" "rejoice", because it has been accomplished according to their intentions. Therefore, it is extensively stated in the sūtras that for a bodhisattva, the arising of anger for even an instant is a greater fault than the arising of the fault of attachment for an eon, because it contradicts compassion in every way; and in particular, anger directed toward the object of a bodhisattva is a great fault. As it is said in the Dharma discourse of the Ratnakūṭa called Maitreyamahāsiṃhanāda: "One should flee a hundred yojanas away from a place with angry disputes; one should not generate an angry mind. Fighting and generating an angry mind toward another bodhisattva is a far heavier fault than scolding, striking, and attacking with weapons all the sentient beings of the great trichiliocosm, and by it a bodhisattva is wounded and degenerates; for example, just as iron is not cut by things other than iron such as clods of earth and so forth, the roots of virtue of a bodhisattva are also exhausted by anger toward another bodhisattva, whereas they cannot be exhausted by other things; therefore, they should treat one another with reverence and respect, and one should generate the perception of the Teacher even toward a bodhisattva who has first generated the mind."

གཅིག་གིས་གཅིག་ལ་ཞེ་ས་དང་གུས་པ་དང་བཅས་པར་བྱ་སྟེ་སེམས་དང་པོ་བསྐྱེད་པའི་བྱང་ཆུབ་སེམས་དཔའ་ལ་ཡང་སྟོན་པའི་འདུ་ཤེས་བསྐྱེད་པར་བྱའོ། །ཞེས་གསུངས་པ་བཞིན་ནོ།

First, two verses starting with "Whenever bodhisattvas": Although māras do not find an opportunity against a bodhisattva who is endowed with skillful means and the armor of wisdom as explained above, they do find an opportunity against those of lesser capacity who are not endowed with that method. Furthermore, the Aṣṭasāhasrikā mentions seven faults by which māras find an opportunity, and the Pañcaviṃśatisāhasrikā mentions twelve; what is taught here is the last of them: "At" "which" "time" "bodhisattvas" "fight" with their bodies "and" "dispute" with their speech with one another, "and", in mutual "disharmony", "become" "endowed" "with" "angry" minds, "at" "that" "time", the sinful "māras" "rejoice", "and" however much the dispute increases, to that extent they "become" "supremely" "joyful"; the reason for that is because they "think": "Due to the fault of that dispute, which contradicts the path of skillful means and wisdom, 'both' of 'those' bodhisattvas 'become' 'distant' 'from' the 'wisdom' 'of' the 'Victorious' 'Ones', and we have found an opportunity." In this way, "both" of "them" "become" "distant" from the wisdom of a Buddha, "and", with untamed mindstreams, they "become" "like" "flesh-eating" demons, such as rākṣasas and pretas. "Both" the one who gets angry and the one who retaliates against anger "will" "violate", through dispute, "their" "own" "vow" to attain perfect awakening out of compassion for the sake of others and to practice its path, the perfections; for disputing with anger contradicts in every way compassion, bodhicitta, the wisdom that sees selflessness, and so forth. For one who "hates" "and" is "devoid" "of" its antidote, "patience", "how" "could" "there" "be" the attainment of "awakening"? It is like a sprout from a burnt seed. "At" "that" "time", when such dispute has occurred, the "māras", "together" "with" those who belong to their "own" "partisan" side, "will" "rejoice", because it has been accomplished according to their intentions. Therefore, it is extensively stated in the sūtras that for a bodhisattva, the arising of anger for even an instant is a greater fault than the arising of the fault of attachment for an eon, because it contradicts compassion in every way; and in particular, anger directed toward the object of a bodhisattva is a great fault. As it is said in the Dharma discourse of the Ratnakūṭa called Maitreyamahāsiṃhanāda: "One should flee a hundred yojanas away from a place with angry disputes; one should not generate an angry mind. Fighting and generating an angry mind toward another bodhisattva is a far heavier fault than scolding, striking, and attacking with weapons all the sentient beings of the great trichiliocosm, and by it a bodhisattva is wounded and degenerates; for example, just as iron is not cut by things other than iron such as clods of earth and so forth, the roots of virtue of a bodhisattva are also exhausted by anger toward another bodhisattva, whereas they cannot be exhausted by other things; therefore, they should treat one another with reverence and respect, and one should generate the perception of the Teacher even toward a bodhisattva who has first generated the mind."

translation: First, one verse starting with "Buddhas by patience": If the "Buddhas" "touch" "awakening" "by" "the" "perfection" "of" "patience", they "think", "This 'mind' of mine, which is anger, the opposite of that, 'is' 'not' 'good'; it has the nature of burning the roots of virtue from many eons and strongly contradicts the path to awakening." Thus they "generate" "mindfulness" that knows a fault as a fault, "and" being supremely regretful of the sin they committed is the power of revulsion. "In" "order" "to" "confess" that sinful entity "individually", they visualize the Buddhas and bodhisattvas of the ten directions to make them directly present and rely on them, which is the power of support; they engage in any sequence of Dharma practice, such as reading profound sūtras, reciting dhāraṇīs, and resting evenly in the profound meaning, which is the power of the antidote; "and", "later" "also", they "vow" not to commit such a fault, which is the power of restoration. "And" thinking, "Such an untamed thing is not suitable to be done by me, a bodhisattva," by way of a revulsed mind, "whoever" "does" "not" "rejoice" in the nature of dispute and so forth, "they" "train" "in" "this" "Dharma" "of" the "Buddhas", and do not train in the dharma of māras.

Work: ཡོན་ཏན་རིན་ཆེན་སྡུད་པའི་འགྲེལ་པ་རྒྱལ་བའི་ཡུམ་གྱི་དགོངས་དོན་ལ་ཕྱིན་ཅི་མ་ལོག་པར་འཇུག་པའི་ལེགས་བཤད། ('Commentary on Precious Qualities: Entering the True Intent of the Buddha''s Mother'), author: འཇུ་མི་ཕམ།. A canonical Tibetan text; the blocks below are being translated in order.

Preceding blocks of this same document and their translations — match this terminology, register and line shape:

[1-348] source:
གཉིས་པ་ལ་གླགས་མི་རྙེད་པའི་ཚུལ་དང་། ཞར་ལ་ལྡོག་ཕྱོགས་གླགས་རྙེད་པའི་རྒྱུ་བསྟན་པ་གཉིས།
[1-348] translation already produced for this document:
Regarding the second, there are two: how they do not find an opportunity, and incidentally showing the causes for the opposing side finding an opportunity.

[1-349] source:
དང་པོ། གང་ཚེ་མཁས་པ་སོགས་ཚིགས་བཅད་གཅིག་སྟེ། བདུད་ཀྱི་ཆོ་འཕྲུལ་སྟོན་པ་དེ་ལྟར་གྱུར་པ་གང༷་གི༷་ཚེ༷་ན་མཁས༷་པ༷་བྱང་ཆུབ་སེམས་དཔའ་དེ༷་དག༷་ཐེག་པ་ཆེན་པོའི་ལམ་དེ་ལ་མི་ཕྱེད་པའི་བས༷མ་པ་རབ༷་ཏུ་དྲག་པོ་དང་ལྡན༷་ཞིང༷་། སྦྱོར་བའི་སྒོ་ནས་ཉིན༷་མཚ༷ན་རྟག་ཏུ་ཤེས༷་རབ༷་ཀྱི༷་ཕ༷་རོལ༷་ཏུ་ཕྱིན༷་པ༷་མཆོག༷་གི་དོན༷་ལ༷་ལྟ་བར་བྱེད་དོ། །དེ་ལྟར་བྱས་པ་དེ༷་ཡི་ཚེ༷་བྱང་སེམས་དེའི་ལུས༷་དང་སེམ༷ས་ད༷ག་ནི༷་མཁའ༷་ལ་འགྲོ༷་བའི་བྱ༷་ལྟར༷་དུ་སྲིད་ཞིའི་གཡངས་སའི་འཇིགས་པ་མེད་པར་རྒྱུ༷་སྟེ་མི་གནས་པའི་ཤེར་ཕྱིན་ལ་གནས་པའི་མཐུ་ལས་སོ། །དེས་ན་དེ་ལ་ནག༷་པོའི༷་རྩ༷་ལག༷་རྣམ༷ས་ཀྱིས༷་གླགས༷་རྙེད༷་པར་ག༷་ལ༷་འགྱུར༷་ཏེ་ནམ་མཁར་འགྲོ་བའི་བྱ་ལ་ཁྱི་སོགས་ཀྱིས་མི་ཚུགས་པ་བཞིན་ནོ། །
[1-349] translation already produced for this document:
First, one verse starting with "Whenever the learned": "At" "which" "time" the display of the māras' magical emanations occurs like that, "those" "learned" bodhisattvas are "endowed" with an unshakeable and "very" fierce "intention" toward the path of the Mahayana, "and", by way of application, they look "at" the "meaning" of the "supreme" "perfection" "of" "wisdom" constantly, "day" and "night". "At" "that" "time", having done so, "these" "bodies" "and" "minds" of that bodhisattva "travel" without fear of the precipices of existence and peace, "like" a "bird" "going" "in" the "sky"—which is due to the power of abiding in the non-abiding perfection of wisdom. Therefore, "how" "could" an "opportunity" be "found" against them "by" the "dark" "partisans"? It is like how a bird going in the sky cannot be harmed by dogs and so forth.

[1-350] source:
གཉིས་པ་ལ་གླགས་རྙེད་པའི་རྒྱུ་གཙོ་བོ་རྩོད་པ་ཡིན་པར་བསྟན་པ། ཉེས་པ་དེ་ལས་སྡང་བའི་ཐབས་བསྟན་པ་གཉིས།
[1-350] translation already produced for this document:
Regarding the second, there are two: showing that the main cause of finding an opportunity is dispute, and showing the means of despising that fault.

[1-351] source:
དང་པོ་ལ་རྩོད་པ་སྤྱི་དང་། བྱེ་བྲག་ཏུ་ལུང་བསྟན་མ་ཐོབ་པས་ཐོབ་པའི་བྱང་སེམས་ལ་རྩོད་པའི་ཉེས་དམིགས་གཉིས།
[1-351] translation already produced for this document:
Regarding the first, there are two: dispute in general, and specifically, the drawbacks of a bodhisattva who has not obtained a prophecy disputing with a bodhisattva who has obtained it.

[1-352] source:
དང་པོ། གང་ཚེ་བྱང་ཆུབ་སོགས་ཚིགས་བཅད་གཉིས་ཏེ། གོང་དུ་བཤད་པ་ལྟར་ཐབས་མཁས་པ་དང་ཤེས་རབ་ཀྱི་གོ་ཆ་དང་ལྡན་པའི་བྱང་ཆུབ་སེམས་དཔའ་ལ་བདུད་ཀྱི་གླགས་མི་རྙེད་ཀྱང་ཚུལ་དེ་དང་མི་ལྡན་པའི་བློ་ཆུང་བ་ལ་གླགས་རྙེད་པ་ཡིན་ལ། དེ་ཡང་བརྒྱད་སྟོང་པ་ལས། བདུད་ཀྱི་གླགས་རྙེད་པའི་ཉེས་པ་བདུན་དང་། ཉི་ཁྲི་ལས་བཅུ་གཉིས་གསུངས་པའི་ཐ་མ་དེ་འདིར་བསྟན་པ་ནི། དུས་གང༷་གི་ཚེ༷་བྱང༷་ཆུབ༷་སེམ༷ས་དཔའ༷་གང་ཕན་ཚུན་དུ་ལུས་ཀྱིས་འཐབ༷་པ་དང༷་ངག་གིས་རྩོད༷་པར་གྱུར༷་ཅིང༷་། ཕན༷་ཚུན༷་དུ་གཅིག་ལ་གཅིག་མི༷་མཐུན༷་པ་ཁྲོས༷་པའི༷་སེམ༷ས་དང༷་ལྡན༷་པར་གྱུར༷་པ༷་དེ༷་ཡི་ཚེ༷་ན་བདུ༷ད་སྡིག་ཅན་དེ་ནི༷་དགའ༷་ཞིང༷་རྩོད་པ་ཅི་ཙམ་འཕེལ་བ་དེ་ཙམ་དུ་མཆོག༷་ཏུ༷་ཉ༷མས་བདེ༷་བར་འགྱུར༷་ཏེ། དེའི་རྒྱུ་མཚན་བྱང་ཆུབ་སེམས་དཔའ་དེ༷་གཉི༷ས་ཀ་ཐབས་དང་ཤེས་རབ་ཀྱི་ལམ་དང་འགལ་བ་རྩོད་པ་དེའི་ཉེས་པས་རྒྱལ༷་བའི༷་ཡེ༷་ཤེས༷་ལ༷ས་ནི༷་ཐག་རིང༷་དུ་འགྱུར༷་ཞིང་བདག་གིས་གླགས་རྙེད་དོ་སྙམ༷་པའི་ཕྱིར་རོ། །དེ་ལྟར་དེ༷་གཉི༷ས་ཀ་སངས་རྒྱས་ཀྱི་ཡེ་ཤེས་ལས་རིང༷་དུ༷་འགྱུར༷་ཞིང༷་རྒྱུད་མ་རང་པ་སྲིན་པོ་དང་ཡི་དྭགས་ལ་སོགས་པ་ཤ༷་ཟ༷་རྣམས་དང་འདྲ༷་བར༷་འགྱུར༷་ལ། ཁྲོ་བ་དང་ཁྲོ་བ་ལ་སླར་ལན་བྱེད་པ་གཉི༷ས་ཀ༷་ཡང་གཞན་དོན་དུ་སྙིང་རྗེས་རྫོགས་བྱང་ཐོབ་འདོད་དང་དེའི་ལམ་ཕར་ཕྱིན་ཉམས་སུ་ལེན་པར་རང༷་གི༷་དམ༷་བཅས༷་པ་དེ་རྩོད་པས་ཉ༷མས་པར༷་བྱེ༷ད་པར༷་འགྱུར༷་ཏེ། ཁྲོ་བས་རྩོད་པ་ནི་སྙིང་རྗེ་དང་བྱང་ཆུབ་ཀྱི་སེམས་དང་བདག་མེད་པར་མཐོང་བའི་ཤེས་རབ་སོགས་དང་རྣམ་པ་ཀུན་ཏུ་འགལ་བའི་ཕྱིར།ཡིད་སྡང༷་ཞིང༷་དེའི་གཉེན་པོ་བཟོ༷ད་པ་དང༷་བྲལ༷་བ་ལ༷་བྱང༷་ཆུབ༷་ཐོབ་པ་ག༷་ལ༷་ཡོ༷ད་དེ་ས་བོན་བསྲེགས་པའི་མྱུ་གུ་བཞིན་ནོ། །དེ་ལྟར་རྩོད་པར་གྱུར་པ་དེ༷་ཡི་ཚེ༷་བདུ༷ད་རྣམ༷ས་རང་གི་ཕྱོགས༷་སུ་གཏོགས་པ་རྣམས་དང༷་བཅས༷་ཏེ༷་དག༷འ་བར༷་འགྱུར༷་ཏེ་དེ་དག་གི་བསམ་པ་བཞིན་དུ་གྲུབ་པའི་ཕྱིར་རོ། །དེས་ན་བྱང་ཆུབ་སེམས་དཔའ་ལ་འདོད་ཆགས་ཀྱི་ཉེས་པ་བསྐལ་པའི་བར་དུ་བྱུང་བ་ལས་ཁྲོ་བ་སྐད་ཅིག་ཙམ་སྐྱེས་པ་དེ་ནི་སྙིང་རྗེ་དང་རྣམ་པ་ཀུན་ཏུ་འགལ་བའི་ཕྱིར་ཉེས་པ་ཆེ་ཚུལ་མདོ་རྣམས་ལས་རྒྱ་ཆེར་འབྱུང་ལ་ཁྱད་པར་དུ་ཡུལ་བྱང་ཆུབ་སེམས་དཔའ་ལ་ཁྲོ་བ་ནི་ཉེས་པ་ཆེ་སྟེ། བྱམས་པ་སེང་གེ་སྒྲ་ཆེན་པོ་ཞེས་བྱ་བ་དཀོན་མཆོག་བརྩེགས་པའི་ཆོས་ཀྱི་རྣམ་གྲངས་ལས། ཞེ་སྡང་གི་རྩོད་པ་དང་བཅས་པའི་གནས་ལས་དཔག་ཚད་བརྒྱར་འབྱོལ་བར་བྱ་སྟེ། ཞེ་སྡང་གི་སེམས་བསྐྱེད་པར་མི་བྱའོ། །སྟོང་གསུམ་གྱི་སྟོང་ཆེན་པོའི་འཇིག་རྟེན་ཁམས་ཀྱི་སེམས་ཅན་ཐམས་ཅད་ལ་སྤྱོས་ཤིང་བརྡེག་ལ་མཚོན་གྱིས་བཏབ་པ་བས་བྱང་ཆུབ་སེམས་དཔའ་གཞན་ལ་ཐབ་དང་ཞེ་སྡང་གི་སེམས་བསྐྱེད་པ་དེ་ཆེས་ཉེས་པ་ལྕི་ཞིང་དེས་བྱང་ཆུབ་སེམས་དཔའ་སྨས་པ་དང་ཉམས་པར་འགྱུར་ཏེ། First, two verses starting with "Whenever bodhisattvas": Although māras do not find an opportunity against a bodhisattva who is endowed with skillful means and the armor of wisdom as explained above, they do find an opportunity against those of lesser capacity who are not endowed with that method. Furthermore, the Aṣṭasāhasrikā mentions seven faults by which māras find an opportunity, and the Pañcaviṃśatisāhasrikā mentions twelve; what is taught here is the last of them: "At" "which" "time" "bodhisattvas" "fight" with their bodies "and" "dispute" with their speech with one another, "and", in mutual "disharmony", "become" "endowed" "with" "angry" minds, "at" "that" "time", the sinful "māras" "rejoice", "and" however much the dispute increases, to that extent they "become" "supremely" "joyful"; the reason for that is because they "think": "Due to the fault of that dispute, which contradicts the path of skillful means and wisdom, 'both' of 'those' bodhisattvas 'become' 'distant' 'from' the 'wisdom' 'of' the 'Victorious' 'Ones', and we have found an opportunity." In this way, "both" of "them" "become" "distant" from the wisdom of a Buddha, "and", with untamed mindstreams, they "become" "like" "flesh-eating" demons, such as rākṣasas and pretas. "Both" the one who gets angry and the one who retaliates against anger "will" "violate", through dispute, "their" "own" "vow" to attain perfect awakening out of compassion for the sake of others and to practice its path, the perfections; for disputing with anger contradicts in every way compassion, bodhicitta, the wisdom that sees selflessness, and so forth. For one who "hates" "and" is "devoid" "of" its antidote, "patience", "how" "could" "there" "be" the attainment of "awakening"? It is like a sprout from a burnt seed. "At" "that" "time", when such dispute has occurred, the "māras", "together" "with" those who belong to their "own" "partisan" side, "will" "rejoice", because it has been accomplished according to their intentions. Therefore, it is extensively stated in the sūtras that for a bodhisattva, the arising of anger for even an instant is a greater fault than the arising of the fault of attachment for an eon, because it contradicts compassion in every way; and in particular, anger directed toward the object of a bodhisattva is a great fault. As it is said in the Dharma discourse of the Ratnakūṭa called Maitreyamahāsiṃhanāda: "One should flee a hundred yojanas away from a place with angry disputes; one should not generate an angry mind. Fighting and generating an angry mind toward another bodhisattva is a far heavier fault than scolding, striking, and attacking with weapons all the sentient beings of the great trichiliocosm, and by it a bodhisattva is wounded and degenerates; for example, just as iron is not cut by things other than iron such as clods of earth and so forth, the roots of virtue of a bodhisattva are also exhausted by anger toward another bodhisattva, whereas they cannot be exhausted by other things; therefore, they should treat one another with reverence and respect, and one should generate the perception of the Teacher even toward a bodhisattva who has first generated the mind."

"Both" the one who gets angry and the one who retaliates against anger "will" "violate", through dispute, "their" "own" "vow" to attain perfect awakening out of compassion for the sake of others and to practice its path, the perfections; for disputing with anger contradicts in every way compassion, bodhicitta, the wisdom that sees selflessness, and so forth. For one who "hates" "and" is "devoid" "of" its antidote, "patience", "how" "could" "there" "be" the attainment of "awakening"? It is like a sprout from a burnt seed. As it is said in the Dharma discourse of the Ratnakūṭa called Maitreyamahāsiṃhanāda: "One should flee a hundred yojanas away from a place with angry disputes; one should not generate an angry mind. Fighting and generating an angry mind toward another bodhisattva is a far heavier fault than scolding, striking, and attacking with weapons all the sentient beings of the great trichiliocosm, and by it a bodhisattva is wounded and degenerates; for example, just as iron is not cut by things other than iron such as clods of earth and so forth, the roots of virtue of a bodhisattva are also exhausted by anger toward another bodhisattva, whereas they cannot be exhausted by other things; therefore, they should treat one another with reverence and respect, and one should generate the perception of the Teacher even toward a bodhisattva who has first generated the mind."

First, two verses starting with "Whenever bodhisattvas": Although māras do not find an opportunity against a bodhisattva who is endowed with skillful means and the armor of wisdom as explained above, they do find an opportunity against those of lesser capacity who are not endowed with that method. Furthermore, the Aṣṭasāhasrikā mentions seven faults by which māras find an opportunity, and the Pañcaviṃśatisāhasrikā mentions twelve; what is taught here is the last of them: "At" "which" "time" "bodhisattvas" "fight" with their bodies "and" "dispute" with their speech with one another, "and", in mutual "disharmony", "become" "endowed" "with" "angry" minds, "at" "that" "time", the sinful "māras" "rejoice", "and" however much the dispute increases, to that extent they "become" "supremely" "joyful"; the reason for that is because they "think": "Due to the fault of that dispute, which contradicts the path of skillful means and wisdom, 'both' of 'those' bodhisattvas 'become' 'distant' 'from' the 'wisdom' 'of' the 'Victorious' 'Ones', and we have found an opportunity." In this way, "both" of "them" "become" "distant" from the wisdom of a Buddha, "and", with untamed mindstreams, they "become" "like" "flesh-eating" demons, such as rākṣasas and pretas. "Both" the one who gets angry and the one who retaliates against anger "will" "violate", through dispute, "their" "own" "vow" to attain perfect awakening out of compassion for the sake of others and to practice its path, the perfections; for disputing with anger contradicts in every way compassion, bodhicitta, the wisdom that sees selflessness, and so forth. For one who "hates" "and" is "devoid" "of" its antidote, "patience", "how" "could" "there" "be" the attainment of "awakening"? It is like a sprout from a burnt seed. "At" "that" "time", when such dispute has occurred, the "māras", "together" "with" those who belong to their "own" "partisan" side, "will" "rejoice", because it has been accomplished according to their intentions. Therefore, it is extensively stated in the sūtras that for a bodhisattva, the arising of anger for even an instant is a greater fault than the arising of the fault of attachment for an eon, because it contradicts compassion in every way; and in particular, anger directed toward the object of a bodhisattva is a great fault. As it is said in the Dharma discourse of the Ratnakūṭa called Maitreyamahāsiṃhanāda: "One should flee a hundred yojanas away from a place with angry disputes; one should not generate an angry mind. Fighting and generating an angry mind toward another bodhisattva is a far heavier fault than scolding, striking, and attacking with weapons all the sentient beings of the great trichiliocosm, and by it a bodhisattva is wounded and degenerates; for example, just as iron is not cut by things other than iron such as clods of earth and so forth, the roots of virtue of a bodhisattva are also exhausted by anger toward another bodhisattva, whereas they cannot be exhausted by other things; therefore, they should treat one another with reverence and respect, and one should generate the perception of the Teacher even toward a bodhisattva who has first generated the mind."

heading: **དེ་ལྟར་ཤེས་པའི་ཕན་ཡོན།**
translation: Second, two verses starting with "Bodhisattva": "Whoever" is a "bodhisattva" who "knows" "this" "training" of no-more-learning "such" as that, "they" will not "ever"—meaning at any time—"diminish" from the "training" of wisdom and samadhi, nor "will" their "discipline" "be" "impaired", because they have abandoned the view with apprehension which is the cause of faults, just as when there is no poison seed, its leaves and fruits do not grow. Such a bodhisattva, "they", "train" "in" "such" a profound path of wisdom "in" "order" "to" "accomplish" or to "have" "found" the "Dharma" "of" the "Buddhas" such as the powers. Also, it appears to be commented on as for the sake of abiding in the dharma that pleases or delights the Buddhas. That bodhisattva, "they", increase "higher" in the "training" of mind and discipline and "are" "skilled" "in" the "training" of wisdom, and the reason for that is because they abide on a "non-apprehensible" path, for they think that if they were with apprehension, they would be obscured by views of self and so forth, and thus it would not become the higher training. Thus, one should "train" "like" "that" in the "wisdom" "of" "those" bodhisattvas who are "skilled" in the two truths, "making" the "light" of Dharma appearance. When training like that, they "do" "not" "generate" "even" "one" "non-virtuous" "mind" with afflictive conceptualizations that contradict the path to omniscience. Because their mindstream is pervaded by the light of profound wisdom, there is no opportunity for the darkness of bad conceptualizations to remain, "like" how "in" "the" "space" "before" "it", which has "become" "overwhelmed" by the rays of the "sun" "moving" "in" the "sky", "darkness" "does" "not" "remain" entirely.

translation: First, one verse starting with "Perfection of wisdom": "Of" "those" "having" "done" the "training" "in" the "perfection" "of" "wisdom" like this, "all" "perfections" such as generosity "will" "be" "subsumed" "in" "this", their basis of training, the perfection of wisdom, for there is not even a little that is not included within it. Why is that? The perfection of wisdom of the path is genuinely skilled in the way of the two truths; through that wisdom it annihilates the perfections' discordant classes such as miserliness, and through skill in means it does not abandon the result, great awakening; and because it does not conceptualize the three spheres in that either, all paths become the essence of the single perfection endowed with all supreme aspects, and it makes all of them have a single taste in the omniscient aspect of the wisdom of emptiness endowed with all supreme aspects as the result. Therefore, if this perfection of wisdom exists, the trainings of all perfections will be completely present without missing anything, so the arising of all of them in reliance on this root is, for example, the sixty-two views taught in the Brahmajāla Sūtra—the eighteen views relying on the past limit such as the four proclaimers of permanence and so forth, and the forty-four views relying on the future limit such as proclaiming the existence or non-existence of perception, proclaimers of annihilation, and so forth. Since all of them hold the subject, the self, to exist and investigate its various specific qualities, those "sixty-two" "views" are "subsumed" in self-grasping or "in" the "view" "of" the "transitory" "collection", because they arise in reliance on that basis and become mere differentiations of it, and if it does not exist, all the others will not exist either. Knowing that, "like" "that" example, all these perfections are also "taught" to be "subsumed" "in" "this" "perfection" of wisdom.

translation: Second, how it becomes training in all vehicles, one verse starting with "Bodhisattvas skilled": A "bodhisattva" who is "skilled" in the perfection of wisdom becomes skilled in the three vehicles. Just as a bre measure is included in one khal, if one knows this perfection of wisdom which is the supreme path where the aspects of means and wisdom are thoroughly perfected, one knows in passing the path of the śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas which is limited in means and wisdom. Therefore, it is said that the paths of the three vehicles are taught extensively from this perfection of wisdom, and it is taught that those who wish to train in the śrāvaka ground should also train in this. Just as there are various jewels in the treasury of a great king, so the substances needed by the lower ones can also be taken from there. Likewise, the paths and results of those who have entered the path of limited self-interest are deeply known in passing through this. Although that is the case, those bodhisattvas "train" unconfusedly "in" "whatever" "qualities" of the "śrāvaka" training "and" "likewise" "all" "qualities" of the training of the "pratyekabuddhas", and they guide beings of those families through those ways, but "those" bodhisattvas do "not" themselves "abide" "in" "those" lower paths, and "desire" for them "does" "not" "arise" either. translation: The greatness of the person who enters in that way. དང་པོ་སྐྱེ་བོའི་དབུས་ན་སོགས་ཚིགས་བཅད་གཉིས་ཏེ། དེ་ལྟར་མི་རྟོག་པའི་སྤྱོད་ཡུལ་ཐོབ་པ་དེས་སེམས་ཅན་གྱི་དོན་མཛད་པ་སོགས་ཅི་ལྟ་བུ་ཡིན་ཞེ་ན་དཔེའི་སྒོ་ནས་བཤད་པ། དཔེར་ན་ལྟད་མོར་འདུས་པའི་སྐྱེ༷་བོ༷་མང་པོའི་དབུས༷་ན༷་སྒྱུ༷་མའི༷་སྐྱེས༷་བུ༷་སྟེ་སྒྱུ་མའི་སྔགས་སོགས་ཀྱི་མཐུས་སྣང་བའི་སྐྱེས་བུ་དེ་འདི༷་སྙམ༷་དུ༷། བདག་གི་ལྷ་ལ་སོགས་པའི་གཟུགས་སུ་སྣང་བ་འདིས་སྐྱེ༷་བོ༷་མང་པོའི་ཚོགས་འདི༷་མགུ༷་བར་བྱ༷འོ་སྙམ༷་དུ་མི༷་སེམ༷ས་མོད་ཀྱི། ལྟད་མོ་བ་རྣམས་མིག་མགུ་བའི་བྱ་བ་དེ༷་ཡང༷་བྱེ༷ད་དེ་འདི་ལྟར་གཡོ་འགུལ་ལ་སོགས་པའི་རྫུ༷་འཕྲུལ༷་སྣ༷་ཚོགས༷་པ་རབ༷་ཏུ༷་སྟོན༷་པར༷་བྱེ༷ད་པ་སྐྱེ་བོའི་ཚོགས་དེས་མཐོང༷་ན་ཡང༷་། སྒྱུ་མའི་སྐྱེས་བུ་དེ༷་ལ༷་ལུས༷་སུ་གྲུབ་པ་མེ༷ད་ལ་སེམ༷ས་ཀྱང་མེ༷ད་དེ། དེ་ལྟར་གདགས་གཞིས་སྟོང་པ་ལ་མིང༷་ཡང༷་གྲུབ་པ་ཡོ༷ད་པ་མ༷་ཡི༷ན་ནོ། །དེ༷་བཞིན༷་དུ་ཤེས༷་རབ༷་ཀྱི་ཕ་རོལ་ཏུ་ཕྱིན་པ་དམིགས་པ་མེད་པའི་དོན་ལ་སྤྱོ༷ད་པ༷་བྱང་ཆུབ་སེམས་དཔའ་རྟོག་པ་མེད་པ་དག་ནི། ནམ༷་ཡང༷་འདི༷་སྙམ༷་དུ༷་བདག་གིས་བྱང༷་ཆུབ༷་ཆེན་པོ་རྟོག༷ས་པར་བྱས་ནས༷་འགྲོ༷་བ༷་རྣམས་ཡོངས༷་སུ༷་དགྲོལ༷་ལོ་ཞེས་མི༷་སེམ༷ས་མོད་ཀྱི། འཇིག་རྟེན་གྱི་ཁམས་སུ་སྐྱེ༷་བ༷་སྣ༷་ཚོགས༷་པར་སྟོན་པ་དང༷་ནི༷་གདུལ་བྱ་འདུལ་བའི་བྱ༷་བ༷་མང༷་པོ་དང་ལྡན༷་པ༷་དག དཔེར་ན་མེད་བཞིན་སྣང་བ་སྒྱུ༷་མ༷་ལྟ༷་བུར༷་སྟོན༷་ཀྱང༷་དེ་དང་དེར་རྣམ༷་པ༷ར་མི༷་རྟོག༷་པའི་ཚུལ་གྱིས་སྤྱོ༷ད་པ་ཡིན་ནོ། །
[1-372] translation already produced for this document:
First, two verses starting with "In the midst of people": If one asks, "What is it like when one who has thus attained the domain of non-conceptuality works for the benefit of sentient beings and so forth?", it is explained through an example. For example, "in" "the" "midst" of many "people" gathered for a spectacle, an "illusory" "person"—a person who appears by the power of illusory mantras and so forth—certainly does "not" "think" "like" "this": "Through this appearance in the form of a deity or the like, I will "please" "this" host of many "people"." Nevertheless, they "also" "do" "that" action that pleases the eyes of the spectators; even "if" that host of people "sees" them "exhibiting" "various" "miracles" such as moving and shaking in this way, "that" illusory person has "no" "body" established and "no" "mind" either, so being empty of a basis of designation, they do "not" "have" an established "name" "either". "Likewise", non-conceptual bodhisattvas who "practice" the objectless meaning of the perfection of "wisdom" certainly "never" "think" "like" "this": "Having "realized" great "awakening", I will "completely" "liberate" "beings"." Nevertheless, those who manifest "various" "births" in the world realms "and" "possess" "many" "actions" of taming disciples "practice" in a "non-conceptual" manner regarding this and that, even "though" they "manifest" "like" an "illusion"—appearing while not existing, for example.

གཉིས་པ། དཔེར་ན་སངས་རྒྱས་སོགས་ཚིགས་བཅད་གཅིག་སྟེ། དཔེར༷་ན༷་དེ་བཞིན་གཤེགས་པ་ཞི་བའི་བློ་གྲོས་ཀྱི་མཛད་པ་བཞིན་དུ་སངས༷་རྒྱས༷་རྣམས་ཀྱིས་སངས་རྒྱས་སུ་སྤྲུལ༷་པ༷་མཛད་པ་དེ་དག་གིས་ཆོས་སྟོན་པ་སོགས་སངས༷་རྒྱས༷་ཀྱི་མཛ༷ད་པ༷་ཐམས་ཅད་བྱེ༷ད་མོད་ཀྱི། སྤྲུལ་པ་དེས་རང་གི་སངས་རྒྱས་ཀྱི་མཛད་པ་བྱེ༷ད་པ༷་དེ༷་ལ༷་བདག་ནི་སངས་རྒྱས་ཀྱི་མཛད་པ་བྱེད་པའོ་སྙམ་དྲེགས༷་པ༷་ཅུང༷་ཟ༷ད་ཀྱང་སྐྱེ་བར་མི༷་འགྱུར༷་ཏེ་སྤྲུལ་པའི་སྣང་བ་ཙམ་ཡིན་པའི་ཕྱིར་རོ། །དེ༷་བཞིན༷་དུ་ཆོས་ཐམས་ཅད་རང་བཞིན་དབེན་ལ་སྣང་བ་སྒྱུ་མ་ལྟར་རྟོགས་པའི་ཤེས༷་རབ༷་ལ་སྤྱོ༷ད་པ་གོམས་ཤིང་གདིང་དུ་གྱུར་པའི་མཁས༷་པ་མི་རྟོགས་པའི་སྤྱོད་ཡུལ་ཐོབ་པའི་བྱང༷་ཆུབ༷་སེམ༷ས་དཔའ༷་ཡང༷་སྤྲུལ༷་པ༷་དང་སྒྱུ༷་མ༷་བཞིན༷་དུ༷་ཆོས་སྟོན་པ་ལ་སོགས་པའི་བྱ༷་བ༷་ཐམ༷ས་ཅ༷ད་སྟོན༷་ཀྱང་ཀུན་ཏུ་རྟོག་པ་མི་འབྱུང་ངོ་། །

Second, one verse starting with "For example, a Buddha": "For" "example", like the deeds of the Tathāgata Praśāntamati, an "emanation" emanated as a Buddha by the "Buddhas" certainly "performs" all the "deeds" of a "Buddha" such as teaching the Dharma, but "in" "that" "performing" of its own deeds of a Buddha by that emanation, "not" "even" "a" "little" "pride" arises, thinking, "I am performing the deeds of a Buddha," because it is merely the appearance of an emanation. style_instruction: Translate this passage of a Tibetan Buddhist commentary on the Verse Summary of the Perfection of Wisdom (Ratnaguṇasañcayagāthā) into clear, accurate English prose. Translate the whole passage completely and in the same order: do not summarise, shorten or omit anything, and keep the same number of lines as the source. Where the commentary quotes or glosses words of the root verses, keep those quoted words recognisable in the translation. Keep proper names in their standard Sanskrit forms (Subhūti, Śāriputra, Maitreya, Haribhadra) and technical terms recognisable (prajñāpāramitā = perfection of wisdom, bodhisattva). Do not add commentary, notes, or explanation of your own.

Regarding the second, there are three: "not" conceptualizing objects as sentient beings through the example of an illusory person, not conceptualizing an agent through the example of an emanation, and not conceptualizing a result through the example of a carpenter's creation.

[1-372] source:
དང་པོ་སྐྱེ་བོའི་དབུས་ན་སོགས་ཚིགས་བཅད་གཉིས་ཏེ། དེ་ལྟར་མི་རྟོག་པའི་སྤྱོད་ཡུལ་ཐོབ་པ་དེས་སེམས་ཅན་གྱི་དོན་མཛད་པ་སོགས་ཅི་ལྟ་བུ་ཡིན་ཞེ་ན་དཔེའི་སྒོ་ནས་བཤད་པ། དཔེར་ན་ལྟད་མོར་འདུས་པའི་སྐྱེ༷་བོ༷་མང་པོའི་དབུས༷་ན༷་སྒྱུ༷་མའི༷་སྐྱེས༷་བུ༷་སྟེ་སྒྱུ་མའི་སྔགས་སོགས་ཀྱི་མཐུས་སྣང་བའི་སྐྱེས་བུ་དེ་འདི༷་སྙམ༷་དུ༷། བདག་གི་ལྷ་ལ་སོགས་པའི་གཟུགས་སུ་སྣང་བ་འདིས་སྐྱེ༷་བོ༷་མང་པོའི་ཚོགས་འདི༷་མགུ༷་བར་བྱ༷འོ་སྙམ༷་དུ་མི༷་སེམ༷ས་མོད་ཀྱི། ལྟད་མོ་བ་རྣམས་མིག་མགུ་བའི་བྱ་བ་དེ༷་ཡང༷་བྱེ༷ད་དེ་འདི་ལྟར་གཡོ་འགུལ་ལ་སོགས་པའི་རྫུ༷་འཕྲུལ༷་སྣ༷་ཚོགས༷་པ་རབ༷་ཏུ༷་སྟོན༷་པར༷་བྱེ༷ད་པ་སྐྱེ་བོའི་ཚོགས་དེས་མཐོང༷་ན་ཡང༷་། སྒྱུ་མའི་སྐྱེས་བུ་དེ༷་ལ༷་ལུས༷་སུ་གྲུབ་པ་མེ༷ད་ལ་སེམ༷ས་ཀྱང་མེ༷ད་དེ། དེ་ལྟར་གདགས་གཞིས་སྟོང་པ་ལ་མིང༷་ཡང༷་གྲུབ་པ་ཡོ༷ད་པ་མ༷་ཡི༷ན་ནོ། །དེ༷་བཞིན༷་དུ་ཤེས༷་རབ༷་ཀྱི་ཕ་རོལ་ཏུ་ཕྱིན་པ་དམིགས་པ་མེད་པའི་དོན་ལ་སྤྱོ༷ད་པ༷་བྱང་ཆུབ་སེམས་དཔའ་རྟོག་པ་མེད་པ་དག་ནི། ནམ༷་ཡང༷་འདི༷་སྙམ༷་དུ༷་བདག་གིས་བྱང༷་ཆུབ༷་ཆེན་པོ་རྟོག༷ས་པར་བྱས་ནས༷་འགྲོ༷་བ༷་རྣམས་ཡོངས༷་སུ༷་དགྲོལ༷་ལོ་ཞེས་མི༷་སེམ༷ས་མོད་ཀྱི། འཇིག་རྟེན་གྱི་ཁམས་སུ་སྐྱེ༷་བ༷་སྣ༷་ཚོགས༷་པར་སྟོན་པ་དང༷་ནི༷་གདུལ་བྱ་འདུལ་བའི་བྱ༷་བ༷་མང༷་པོ་དང་ལྡན༷་པ༷་དག དཔེར་ན་མེད་བཞིན་སྣང་བ་སྒྱུ༷་མ༷་ལྟ༷་བུར༷་སྟོན༷་ཀྱང༷་དེ་དང་དེར་རྣམ༷་པ༷ར་མི༷་རྟོག༷་པའི་ཚུལ་གྱིས་སྤྱོ༷ད་པ་ཡིན་ནོ། །
[1-372] translation already produced for this document:
First, two verses starting with "In the midst of people": If one asks, "What is it like when one who has thus attained the domain of non-conceptuality works for the benefit of sentient beings and so forth?", it is explained through an example. For example, "in" "the" "midst" of many "people" gathered for a spectacle, an "illusory" "person"—a person who appears by the power of illusory mantras and so forth—certainly does "not" "think" "like" "this": "Through this appearance in the form of a deity or the like, I will "please" "this" host of many "people"." Nevertheless, they "also" "do" "that" action that pleases the eyes of the spectators; even "if" that host of people "sees" them "exhibiting" "various" "miracles" such as moving and shaking in this way, "that" illusory person has "no" "body" established and "no" "mind" either, so being empty of a basis of designation, they do "not" "have" an established "name" "either". "Likewise", non-conceptual bodhisattvas who "practice" the objectless meaning of the perfection of "wisdom" certainly "never" "think" "like" "this": "Having "realized" great "awakening", I will "completely" "liberate" "beings"." Nevertheless, those who manifest "various" "births" in the world realms "and" "possess" "many" "actions" of taming disciples "practice" in a "non-conceptual" manner regarding this and that, even "though" they "manifest" "like" an "illusion"—appearing while not existing, for example.

གཉིས་པ། དཔེར་ན་སངས་རྒྱས་སོགས་ཚིགས་བཅད་གཅིག་སྟེ། དཔེར༷་ན༷་དེ་བཞིན་གཤེགས་པ་ཞི་བའི་བློ་གྲོས་ཀྱི་མཛད་པ་བཞིན་དུ་སངས༷་རྒྱས༷་རྣམས་ཀྱིས་སངས་རྒྱས་སུ་སྤྲུལ༷་པ༷་མཛད་པ་དེ་དག་གིས་ཆོས་སྟོན་པ་སོགས་སངས༷་རྒྱས༷་ཀྱི་མཛ༷ད་པ༷་ཐམས་ཅད་བྱེ༷ད་མོད་ཀྱི། སྤྲུལ་པ་དེས་རང་གི་སངས་རྒྱས་ཀྱི་མཛད་པ་བྱེ༷ད་པ༷་དེ༷་ལ༷་བདག་ནི་སངས་རྒྱས་ཀྱི་མཛད་པ་བྱེད་པའོ་སྙམ་དྲེགས༷་པ༷་ཅུང༷་ཟ༷ད་ཀྱང་སྐྱེ་བར་མི༷་འགྱུར༷་ཏེ་སྤྲུལ་པའི་སྣང་བ་ཙམ་ཡིན་པའི་ཕྱིར་རོ། །དེ༷་བཞིན༷་དུ་ཆོས་ཐམས་ཅད་རང་བཞིན་དབེན་ལ་སྣང་བ་སྒྱུ་མ་ལྟར་རྟོགས་པའི་ཤེས༷་རབ༷་ལ་སྤྱོ༷ད་པ་གོམས་ཤིང་གདིང་དུ་གྱུར་པའི་མཁས༷་པ་མི་རྟོགས་པའི་སྤྱོད་ཡུལ་ཐོབ་པའི་བྱང༷་ཆུབ༷་སེམ༷ས་དཔའ༷་ཡང༷་སྤྲུལ༷་པ༷་དང་སྒྱུ༷་མ༷་བཞིན༷་དུ༷་ཆོས་སྟོན་པ་ལ་སོགས་པའི་བྱ༷་བ༷་ཐམ༷ས་ཅ༷ད་སྟོན༷་ཀྱང་ཀུན་ཏུ་རྟོག་པ་མི་འབྱུང་ངོ་། །

Second, one verse starting with "For example, a Buddha": "For" "example", like the deeds of the Tathāgata Praśāntamati, an "emanation" emanated as a Buddha by the "Buddhas" certainly "performs" all the "deeds" of a "Buddha" such as teaching the Dharma, but "in" "that" "performing" of its own deeds of a Buddha by that emanation, "not" "even" "a" "little" "pride" arises, thinking, "I am performing the deeds of a Buddha," because it is merely the appearance of an emanation. Where the commentary quotes or glosses words of the root verses, keep those quoted words recognisable in the translation. Keep proper names in their standard Sanskrit forms (Subhūti, Śāriputra, Maitreya, Haribhadra) and technical terms recognisable (prajñāpāramitā = perfection of wisdom, bodhisattva). Do not add commentary, notes, or explanation of your own.

[1-383] translation already produced for this document:
First, two verses starting with "The dharmadhātu and thusness": If one asks what the abiding of a bodhisattva is, it is abiding in the perfection of wisdom. What is that like? Since no phenomenon whatsoever is observed other than the dharmadhātu, all phenomena simply become the nature of the dharmadhātu. Having known this, the convention of "the mind abiding in the dharmadhātu" also means not abiding in anything. Since thatness, which is free from all reference points, is designated as the dharmadhātu, there is no basis to be observed in it. Therefore, they "do" "not" "abide" in a referential manner even "in" the reality of entities, the "dharmadhātu", or "thusness", "and" since that is not abiding in anything, it is conventionally called "the abiding of non-abiding". That exalted wisdom that realizes the emptiness of all referential domains as equality "abides" "without" "abiding" in any phenomenon, "for" "example", "like" a "cloud" "in" the "sky" that does not rely on anything.

heading: **མདོར་བསྟན།**
translation: First, one verse starting with "This is the dharma treasure": "This" perfection of wisdom is the source of all the inexhaustible dharmas to be explained by the Buddhas of the three times; thus it is the "supreme" great "treasure" "of" "Dharma", "and" since the precious qualities of the result—the strengths and so forth—arise, and all the various jewels of the qualities of the path—the perfections, dhāraṇīs, factors of awakening, and so forth—also arise, it "is" the marvelous, "sublime" "treasury" "of" vast "Dharma", and it is the "lineage" from which "all" "Buddhas" arise, because they are born from it. It is the "treasury" where all the physical and mental "happiness" "and" "joy" "of" "beings" "abide"; for from the realization of this very profound perfection of wisdom arise all profound and vast dharmas, and however many excellent paths there are, up to worldly right view, arise. One should understand that however many worldly and supramundane excellences there are arise by way of observing the base perfection of wisdom, by way of practicing the path perfection of wisdom, and from obtaining the result perfection of wisdom; in the manner of concomitance, if it is absent they are all averted, and if it is present they are present. "Although" "all" "those" "Protectors" "of" the "world" in the "ten" "directions", however many "Buddhas" there are, "past", "future", "and" those residing now, "are" "born" "from" practicing "this" perfection of wisdom, the "dharmadhātu" that constitutes its essence is never "exhausted", remaining free from decrease and increase. Moreover, if the base perfection of wisdom were absent, there would be no practicing it having realized it properly; and if the path were absent, there would of course be no result; but one should know the way that the "wisdom" that realizes and teaches as it is the base dharmadhātu—the non-dual meaning abiding as the lineage or dharmatā—is also the cause. Second, three verses starting with "the liberation of the arhats": "Except" for the abiding of the "Tathāgata" himself, who abides in the excellent samādhi of "liberation" that has "destroyed" the "enemies" of the two obscurations, "this" "abiding" of the bodhisattva is "supreme" "among" "all" the abidings of other "śrāvakas" "and" "pratyekabuddhas", "however" "many" there are, "endowed" "with" the undefiled "bliss" of the "utterly" "peaceful" "samādhi" where all afflictions are "pacified", "and" since those others are "not" "above" this, this is the unsurpassable abiding. translation: Second, one verse starting with "Sons of the Buddhas and": The "sons" of the "Buddhas"—the bodhisattvas—"and" the "śrāvakas", the "pratyekabuddhas", "and" the "gods", "and" the other "beings", humans and so forth, "all" of their "happiness" "and" joyous "dharmas", "however" "many" there are, "all" "these" "arise" "from" the "supreme" "perfection" "of" "wisdom". If worldly right view is absent, all worldly happiness will also not be accomplished, thus it will not arise; let alone the authentic supramundane path and result. Alternatively, the perfection of wisdom means unsurpassable wisdom; that is the intellect that engages unerringly, exactly as it is, in the nature of the two truths. Thus, all intellects that are unerring regarding the way of the two truths are also included within it and belong to its parts, so all wisdoms that accomplish higher states and definite goodness also depend on it, directly or indirectly. Second, one verse starting with "Sons of the Buddhas and": The "sons" of the "Buddhas"—the bodhisattvas—"and" the "śrāvakas", the "pratyekabuddhas", "and" the "gods", "and" the other "beings", humans and so forth, "all" of their "happiness" "and" joyous "dharmas", "however" "many" there are, "all" "these" "arise" "from" the "supreme" "perfection" "of" "wisdom". For, Buddhas arise from the perfection of wisdom, and from their teaching the Dharma, all the qualities of higher states and definite goodness arise; whereas, without their teaching it, one would definitely not even give rise to the worldly right view that understands the cause and effect of virtue and non-virtue, because one is unable to know them by one's own power alone. If worldly right view is absent, all worldly happiness will also not be accomplished, thus it will not arise; let alone the authentic supramundane path and result. Alternatively, the perfection of wisdom means unsurpassable wisdom; that is the intellect that engages unerringly, exactly as it is, in the nature of the two truths. Thus, all intellects that are unerring regarding the way of the two truths are also included within it and belong to its parts, so all wisdoms that accomplish higher states and definite goodness also depend on it, directly or indirectly. In this way, although all the happiness of saṃsāra and nirvāṇa arises from the perfection of wisdom, "for" "that" "wisdom" there is "never" "exhaustion" or "increase", remaining just as it is.

translation: Explaining the perfection of meditative concentration. translation: Second, one verse starting with "Likewise, the bodhisattva": "Likewise", "the wise" "bodhisattvas" who "give" temporary "joy" "and" ultimate "bliss" to sentient beings, "having" "attained" the "four" "peaceful" "meditative" "absorptions" of "concentration" which pacify the flaws of discordant factors, without becoming attached to being "endowed" with the "bliss" of "concentration", "let" "go" of the "attained" "meditative" "absorptions" of "concentration" which result in rebirth there. "Endowed" "with" "compassion" "for" "beings", they "enter" "back" into the "desire" "realm" because, since there is much suffering in this desire realm, it invigorates the objective focuses for purifying the field; and since there are recipients for accomplishing the perfections, the accumulations are swiftly perfected; and since by teaching the Dharma one can make sentient beings feel renunciation and ripen them, bodhisattvas desiring to swiftly attain buddhahood are born in this desire realm because the accumulations are swiftly perfected here. Concluding by way of the manner in which they become supreme or inferior due to differences in intention.

heading: **སྤང་བྱ།**
translation: First, one verse starting with "The bodhisattva": "If" an "unskillful" "bodhisattva" "counts" the measure in "tens of millions" of "eons" and so on, thinking, 'If I exert myself for this long, I will attain unexcelled awakening,' and, with a "perception" of such a duration as "long" and a perception of "suffering" with respect to difficult practices such as giving away one's head and limbs, "accomplishes" "awakening", "at" "that" "time", while "accomplishing" the "true" "Dharma", unexcelled awakening, through the power of those very perceptions, they "will" "suffer" for a "long" "time". "By" "this", they "degenerate" from the "perfection" of "diligence" and become "lazy". This is because the nature of diligence is joy in virtue, and if one has that joy, one is able to engage in that action without shrinking back, whereas through perceptions of a long time and so on, one's joy degenerates and one becomes discouraged. Even in the world, when one has intense joy for a certain purpose, one gladly travels even on a path of a hundred yojanas, whereas when one is without joy, one looks with dread even upon traveling a single krośa. Therefore, through that skill in means wherein the wisdom that realizes the absence of nature and great compassion enter into union, one should generate the limitless and boundless mind that thinks, 'I shall accomplish perfection, maturation, and purification boundlessly and limitlessly, equally with the boundary that reaches the limit of the boundless realms of sentient beings!' This is the armor-like diligence of a bodhisattva, and by engaging through such armor, as one becomes accustomed to the path, diligence increases accordingly, and its limit becomes immeasurable. Having understood this in accordance with the liberations of Mañjuśrī and others, one should engage in this way.

translation: First, one verse starting with "Toward supreme awakening": Thus, the manner of exerting oneself in diligence that abandons the perception of time as long and the perception of things as difficult to do is as follows: "Taking" as a starting point whichever was the "first" "generation of the mind" "toward" "supreme" "awakening", "until" one finally "attains" "unexcelled" "awakening", "if" one "thinks" "in" one's "mind" that all this duration is easy to pass, like, for example, "the measure" of "a single" "day" "and" "night", and one becomes joyful, "one" "should" "know" that such a manner of "exerting" "diligence" is "by" the "luminous" wisdom of the "wise". If, despite having continuously experienced unbearable suffering in this saṃsāra without beginning since prior eons, one feels no weariness even though that has accomplished no benefit whatsoever, whereas now if one accomplishes this path that establishes the great purpose and ultimate result, it is suitable to be accomplished and progresses increasingly well, so thinking 'why generate weariness toward this?' one becomes joyful; through the power of that, the perceptions of long duration and difficulty are outshined, and thus, through the manner of a perception of short duration even toward a long duration, one's diligence will increase by way of bliss, without suffering. This will be just like, for example, upon seeing the profit of jewels, one does not think of a long and difficult path as difficult, but generates a perception of bliss. Therefore, one should know that whether something is difficult to do or not difficult to do comes about through the power of the mind, independent of the things to be done. This is like bodhisattvas generating joy and a perception of bliss even toward giving away their bodies or entering the Avīci hell for the sake of others.

First, one verse starting with "Toward supreme awakening": Thus, the manner of exerting oneself in diligence that abandons the perception of time as long and the perception of things as difficult to do is as follows: "Taking" as a starting point whichever was the "first" "generation of the mind" "toward" "supreme" "awakening", "until" one finally "attains" "unexcelled" "awakening", "if" one "thinks" "in" one's "mind" that all this duration is easy to pass, like, for example, "the measure" of "a single" "day" "and" "night", and one becomes joyful, "one" "should" "know" that such a manner of "exerting" "diligence" is "by" the "luminous" wisdom of the "wise". If, despite having continuously experienced unbearable suffering in this saṃsāra without beginning since prior eons, one feels no weariness even though that has accomplished no benefit whatsoever, whereas now if one accomplishes this path that establishes the great purpose and ultimate result, it is suitable to be accomplished and progresses increasingly well, so thinking 'why generate weariness toward this?' one becomes joyful; through the power of that, the perceptions of long duration and difficulty are outshined, and thus, through the manner of a perception of short duration even toward a long duration, one's diligence will increase by way of bliss, without suffering. This will be just like, for example, upon seeing the profit of jewels, one does not think of a long and difficult path as difficult, but generates a perception of bliss. style_instruction: Translate this passage of a Tibetan Buddhist commentary on the Verse Summary of the Perfection of Wisdom (Ratnaguṇasañcayagāthā) into clear, accurate English prose. Translate the whole passage completely and in the same order: do not summarise, shorten or omit anything, and keep the same number of lines as the source. Where the commentary quotes or glosses words of the root verses, keep those quoted words recognisable in the translation. Keep proper names in their standard Sanskrit forms (Subhūti, Śāriputra, Maitreya, Haribhadra) and technical terms recognisable (prajñāpāramitā = perfection of wisdom, bodhisattva). Do not add commentary, notes, or explanation of your own.

Even 'when' a bodhisattva 'engages' in conduct, in all lifetimes they 'will' 'attain' 'boundless' 'enjoyments' as much as they desire due to their abundance, 'and' inexhaustible, increasing 'vastness', and having gathered them 'through' the 'generosity' of material things and Dharma, they 'completely' 'ripen' 'sentient beings' 'who' 'are' situated in the causes and results of 'suffering'.

translation: Second, one verse starting with "Having completely perfected this Dharma": Whoever abides in the Mahayana family, starting from when they first generate the mind of awakening, they practice "this" "Dharma" of the Mahayana path, the six perfections as explained, without exception, for three countless eons and so forth in a manner of skillful means. What is skillful means in that? It is rolling all those perfections into a single meaning without separating them, such that they mutually act as friends to one another, and practicing all of them perfectly within each one, and also practicing them in a manner where all of them become the essence of the perfection of wisdom endowed with all supreme aspects. By practicing in that way, "having" "completely" "perfected" the practice of all perfections to the utmost limit, that "bodhisattva" attains the great exalted wisdom at the end of the continuum of the tenth ground, which is able to actualize the dharmadhatu endowed with all supreme aspects, in which all undefiled phenomena are completely perfect, through the exalted wisdom endowed with a single instant. Relying on that, that learner becomes a non-learner, becoming manifestly perfectly a Buddha on the ground of great awakening, and by the power of having found the ultimate transformation of basis, thus, they "completely" "hold" a "completely" "pure" "buddhafield" that reaches the limits of space, without being partial or restricted, the naturally appearing realm of Akaniṣṭha, "and" as retinue, completely "pure" "sentient" "beings" as its contents, the great bodhisattvas of the tenth "ground". And, by attaining the body of exalted wisdom that has become equal to "all" "Buddhas", they completely hold the "continuum" of a Buddha, the nature of the three bodies demonstrating as a teacher in the ten directions of world systems for as long as infinite space exists, possessing a character that is without limits of direction "and" ends of time; "and" they "also" "completely" "hold" the "continuum" "of" the mode of "Dharma" of transmission and realization, which is without boundaries or limits; "likewise", the "continuum" of the noble "Sangha" practicing that Dharma of the Buddha in the world systems of the ten directions, which is without boundaries "and" limits, and they "completely" "hold" "all" "phenomena" of benefit and happiness belonging to existence and peace through great enlightened activity. They attain the ultimate result, the exalted wisdom body extending to the limits of the dharmadhatu, which has reached the culmination of abandonment and realization, is permanent, steadfast, and unchanging like space, and, like a wish-fulfilling jewel, performs benefit and happiness for as long as the boundaries and limits of samsara exist through spontaneously present great enlightened activity.

[1-476] translation already produced for this document:
The specific results of the path. First, sixteen lines or four verses starting with 'By the generosity of a bodhisattva' demonstrate this: Thus, there is no path of a bodhisattva that is not included within the six perfections, and therefore it is said that the Great Vehicle and the extensive texts of the perfection of wisdom are also implicitly included within them. Having well demonstrated the practices of such six perfections above, now their results are explained: 'By' the 'generosity' 'of' a 'bodhisattva', they 'cut' off the continuum of birth in the 'destinies' of 'hungry ghosts', 'and' 'poverty' in enjoyments; 'likewise', they 'cut' off 'all' 'afflictions' as well. By giving objectless generosity themselves, they abandon all afflictions such as miserliness and ignorance, and by giving the generosity of Dharma to others, they cut off all their afflictions too. translation: Third, concluding with the necessity for teaching in that way: one verse starting with "Curing the illnesses of beings": The Buddha is "the" "supreme" "physician" "who" "cures" "the" "illnesses" of body and mind "of" "beings" without exception by means of pacifying them from the root. This is because the Tathāgatas cure the root of all suffering that has become illness, which is the apprehension of entities, along with all afflictions arising from that, and all destitution of existence and peace arising from afflictive and cognitive obscurations, by means of the nectar of the Dharma of the perfection of wisdom. As for the "name" of this sutra, because it contains and gathers in here all the precious "qualities" of the mundane and supramundane paths and results without exception, it is called *The "Precious" "Summary" of "Qualities", "the" "Path" "to" "Supreme" "Awakening"*. As for the necessity of teaching it in that way, it was "explained" "so" "that" "all" the boundless "sentient" "beings" "would" "attain" "this" kind of "path". And as the evidence of completely fulfilling his pledge from countless eons past, "I shall become manifestly awakened in order to completely protect sentient beings," out of objectless great compassion, by teaching this ultimate profound Dharma that he had realized in his own mind to those to be tamed, the close disciples of that time heard it directly from his mouth, and the distant disciples also heard it through transmission. By hearing it in that way they gained focus, by reflecting they understood the meaning, and by meditating they experienced it, gradually becoming Buddhas. ཚུལ་ཁྲིམས༷་ཀྱིས༷་དུད༷་འགྲོ༷འི་འགྲོ༷་བ༷་རིགས་དང་གཟུགས་ལ་སོགས་པ་ཐ་དད་པ་སྣ་ཚོགས་སུ་གྱུར་པ་དུ༷་མའི༷་ངོ༷་བོ༷་དང༷་། དེར་མ་ཟད་མི༷་ཁོམས༷་པའི་གནས་བརྒྱ༷ད་ཆར་ཡང་སྤོང༷་བར་བྱེད་ཅིང་ཁྲིམས་དེ༷་ཡིས༷་དལ༷་བ༷་ཡིརྟེན་བཟང་པོ་རྟག༷་ཏུ༷་རྙེད༷་པར་བྱེད་དོ། །བཟོ༷ད་པས༷་ནི་གཟུགས༷་བཟང༷་བའི་དམ༷་པ༷་རྒྱ༷་ཆེན༷་པོ་མཚན་དཔེས་ལེགས་པར་བརྒྱན་པ་སངས་རྒྱས་ཀྱི་སྐུ་ཡི་བར་དུ་ཐོབ༷་པར་འགྱུར༷་ཏེ༷། གསེར༷་གྱི་མདོག་ལྟ་བུར་སྡུག༷་ཅིང༷་འགྲོ་བས༷་ལྟ༷་བར་བྱ་བའི༷་འོས༷་སུ༷་འགྱུར༷་རོ། །བརྩོན༷་འགྲུས༷་ཀྱིས༷་ནི༷་དཀར༷་པོའི༷་ཆོས་རྣམ༷ས་ཀྱི་ཡོན༷་ཏན༷་འགྲིབ༷་པར་མི༷་འགྱུར༷་བར་གོང་ནས་གོང་དུ་འཕེལ་བའི་མཐུས། ཡེ༷་ཤེས༷་མཐའ༷་ཡས༷་པ་རྒྱལ༷་བའི༷་ཡོན་ཏན་གྱི་བང༷་མཛོད༷་རྙེད༷་པར༷་འགྱུར༷་རོ། །བས༷མ་གཏན༷་གྱིས༷་ནི༷་འདོ༷ད་པའི༷་ཁམས་ཀྱི་འདོད་པའི་ཡོན༷་ཏན༷་ཉེས་དམིགས་ཆེ་ཞིང་བདེ་བ་ཆུང་བས་སྨད༷་པ༷་དག་གི་འོས་སུ་གྱུར་པ་འདོར༷་བར་བྱེད་ཅིང་། སྔོན་གནས་དང་ཟག་ཟད་དང་སེམས་ཤེས་ཏེ་རིག༷་པ་གསུམ་དང༷་། ལྷའི་རྣ་བ་དང་མིག་དང་རྫུ་འཕྲུལ་ཏེ་མངོ༷ན་པར༷་ཤེས༷་པ་གསུམ་སྟེ་སྔ་མ་དང༷་བསྡོམ་པས་དྲུག་པོ་དེ་དང་སེང་གེ་རྣམ་པར་བསྒྱིངས་པ་ལ་སོགས་པའི་ཏིང༷་ངེ་འཛིན༷་མངོ༷ན་པར༷་སྒྲུབ༷་པར་བྱེད་དོ། །ཤེས༷་རབ༷་ཀྱིས༷་ནི༷་ཆོས༷་ཐམས་ཅད་ཀྱི༷་རང༷་བཞིན༷་སྟོང་པ་ཉིད་ཡོངས༷་སུ་ཤེས༷་ནས༷་དངོས་པོར་འཛིན་པ་སྤངས་ཏེ་ཁ༷མས་གསུམ༷་མ༷་ལུས༷་པ༷་ལ༷ས་ཡང༷་དག༷་པར་འདའ༷་བར༷་འགྱུར༷་ལ། སྐུ་གཉིས་དང་ལྡན་པ་མི༷་ཡི༷་ཁྱུ༷་མཆོག༷་ཆོས་ཀྱི་རྒྱལ་པོ་སངས་རྒྱས་སུ་གྱུར་ཏེ་འཇིག་རྟེན་གྱི་ཁམས་ཀུན་ཏུ་མངའ་དབང་བསྒྱུར་བའི་ཕྲིན་ལས་ཀྱི་འཁོར༷་ལོ༷་རིན༷་པོ་ཆེ༷་རྒྱུན་མི་འཆད་པར་བསྐོར༷་བར་བྱས༷་ནས༷་སྡུག༷་བསྔལ༷་མཐའ་དག་གཏན་དུ་ཟ༷ད་པར༷་བྱ༷་བའི་ཕྱིར༷་འགྲོ༷་བ་རྣམས་ལ༷་དམ་པའི་ཆོས༷་ཀྱི་སྣང་བ་མཆོག་ཀྱང༷་སྟོན༷་པར་འགྱུར་རོ། །༈ལམ་ཡོངས་སུ་རྫོགས་པའི་འབྲས་བུ།

Second, one verse starting with "Having completely perfected this Dharma": Whoever abides in the Mahayana family, starting from when they first generate the mind of awakening, they practice "this" "Dharma" of the Mahayana path, the six perfections as explained, without exception, for three countless eons and so forth in a manner of skillful means. What is skillful means in that? It is rolling all those perfections into a single meaning without separating them, such that they mutually act as friends to one another, and practicing all of them perfectly within each one, and also practicing them in a manner where all of them become the essence of the perfection of wisdom endowed with all supreme aspects. By practicing in that way, "having" "completely" "perfected" the practice of all perfections to the utmost limit, that "bodhisattva" attains the great exalted wisdom at the end of the continuum of the tenth ground, which is able to actualize the dharmadhatu endowed with all supreme aspects, in which all undefiled phenomena are completely perfect, through the exalted wisdom endowed with a single instant. Relying on that, that learner becomes a non-learner, becoming manifestly perfectly a Buddha on the ground of great awakening, and by the power of having found the ultimate transformation of basis, thus, they "completely" "hold" a "completely" "pure" "buddhafield" that reaches the limits of space, without being partial or restricted, the naturally appearing realm of Akaniṣṭha, "and" as retinue, completely "pure" "sentient" "beings" as its contents, the great bodhisattvas of the tenth "ground". And, by attaining the body of exalted wisdom that has become equal to "all" "Buddhas", they completely hold the "continuum" of a Buddha, the nature of the three bodies demonstrating as a teacher in the ten directions of world systems for as long as infinite space exists, possessing a character that is without limits of direction "and" ends of time; "and" they "also" "completely" "hold" the "continuum" "of" the mode of "Dharma" of transmission and realization, which is without boundaries or limits; "likewise", the "continuum" of the noble "Sangha" practicing that Dharma of the Buddha in the world systems of the ten directions, which is without boundaries "and" limits, and they "completely" "hold" "all" "phenomena" of benefit and happiness belonging to existence and peace through great enlightened activity. They attain the ultimate result, the exalted wisdom body extending to the limits of the dharmadhatu, which has reached the culmination of abandonment and realization, is permanent, steadfast, and unchanging like space, and, like a wish-fulfilling jewel, performs benefit and happiness for as long as the boundaries and limits of samsara exist through spontaneously present great enlightened activity.

ཚུལ་ཁྲིམས༷་ཀྱིས༷་དུད༷་འགྲོ༷འི་འགྲོ༷་བ༷་རིགས་དང་གཟུགས་ལ་སོགས་པ་ཐ་དད་པ་སྣ་ཚོགས་སུ་གྱུར་པ་དུ༷་མའི༷་ངོ༷་བོ༷་དང༷་། དེར་མ་ཟད་མི༷་ཁོམས༷་པའི་གནས་བརྒྱ༷ད་ཆར་ཡང་སྤོང༷་བར་བྱེད་ཅིང་ཁྲིམས་དེ༷་ཡིས༷་དལ༷་བ༷་ཡིརྟེན་བཟང་པོ་རྟག༷་ཏུ༷་རྙེད༷་པར་བྱེད་དོ། །བཟོ༷ད་པས༷་ནི་གཟུགས༷་བཟང༷་བའི་དམ༷་པ༷་རྒྱ༷་ཆེན༷་པོ་མཚན་དཔེས་ལེགས་པར་བརྒྱན་པ་སངས་རྒྱས་ཀྱི་སྐུ་ཡི་བར་དུ་ཐོབ༷་པར་འགྱུར༷་ཏེ༷། གསེར༷་གྱི་མདོག་ལྟ་བུར་སྡུག༷་ཅིང༷་འགྲོ་བས༷་ལྟ༷་བར་བྱ་བའི༷་འོས༷་སུ༷་འགྱུར༷་རོ། །བརྩོན༷་འགྲུས༷་ཀྱིས༷་ནི༷་དཀར༷་པོའི༷་ཆོས་རྣམ༷ས་ཀྱི་ཡོན༷་ཏན༷་འགྲིབ༷་པར་མི༷་འགྱུར༷་བར་གོང་ནས་གོང་དུ་འཕེལ་བའི་མཐུས། ཡེ༷་ཤེས༷་མཐའ༷་ཡས༷་པ་རྒྱལ༷་བའི༷་ཡོན་ཏན་གྱི་བང༷་མཛོད༷་རྙེད༷་པར༷་འགྱུར༷་རོ། །བས༷མ་གཏན༷་གྱིས༷་ནི༷་འདོ༷ད་པའི༷་ཁམས་ཀྱི་འདོད་པའི་ཡོན༷་ཏན༷་ཉེས་དམིགས་ཆེ་ཞིང་བདེ་བ་ཆུང་བས་སྨད༷་པ༷་དག་གི་འོས་སུ་གྱུར་པ་འདོར༷་བར་བྱེད་ཅིང་། སྔོན་གནས་དང་ཟག་ཟད་དང་སེམས་ཤེས་ཏེ་རིག༷་པ་གསུམ་དང༷་། ལྷའི་རྣ་བ་དང་མིག་དང་རྫུ་འཕྲུལ་ཏེ་མངོ༷ན་པར༷་ཤེས༷་པ་གསུམ་སྟེ་སྔ་མ་དང༷་བསྡོམ་པས་དྲུག་པོ་དེ་དང་སེང་གེ་རྣམ་པར་བསྒྱིངས་པ་ལ་སོགས་པའི་ཏིང༷་ངེ་འཛིན༷་མངོ༷ན་པར༷་སྒྲུབ༷་པར་བྱེད་དོ། །ཤེས༷་རབ༷་ཀྱིས༷་ནི༷་ཆོས༷་ཐམས་ཅད་ཀྱི༷་རང༷་བཞིན༷་སྟོང་པ་ཉིད་ཡོངས༷་སུ་ཤེས༷་ནས༷་དངོས་པོར་འཛིན་པ་སྤངས་ཏེ་ཁ༷མས་གསུམ༷་མ༷་ལུས༷་པ༷་ལ༷ས་ཡང༷་དག༷་པར་འདའ༷་བར༷་འགྱུར༷་ལ། སྐུ་གཉིས་དང་ལྡན་པ་མི༷་ཡི༷་ཁྱུ༷་མཆོག༷་ཆོས་ཀྱི་རྒྱལ་པོ་སངས་རྒྱས་སུ་གྱུར་ཏེ་འཇིག་རྟེན་གྱི་ཁམས་ཀུན་ཏུ་མངའ་དབང་བསྒྱུར་བའི་ཕྲིན་ལས་ཀྱི་འཁོར༷་ལོ༷་རིན༷་པོ་ཆེ༷་རྒྱུན་མི་འཆད་པར་བསྐོར༷་བར་བྱས༷་ནས༷་སྡུག༷་བསྔལ༷་མཐའ་དག་གཏན་དུ་ཟ༷ད་པར༷་བྱ༷་བའི་ཕྱིར༷་འགྲོ༷་བ་རྣམས་ལ༷་དམ་པའི་ཆོས༷་ཀྱི་སྣང་བ་མཆོག་ཀྱང༷་སྟོན༷་པར་འགྱུར་རོ། །༈ལམ་ཡོངས་སུ་རྫོགས་པའི་འབྲས་བུ།
