Second, one verse starting with "Having completely perfected this Dharma": Whoever abides in the Mahayana family, starting from when they first generate the mind of awakening, they practice "this" "Dharma" of the Mahayana path, the six perfections as explained, without exception, for three countless eons and so forth in a manner of skillful means. What is skillful means in that? It is rolling all those perfections into a single meaning without separating them, such that they mutually act as friends to one another, and practicing all of them perfectly within each one, and also practicing them in a manner where all of them become the essence of the perfection of wisdom endowed with all supreme aspects. By practicing in that way, "having" "completely" "perfected" the practice of all perfections to the utmost limit, that "bodhisattva" attains the great exalted wisdom at the end of the continuum of the tenth ground, which is able to actualize the dharmadhatu endowed with all supreme aspects, in which all undefiled phenomena are completely perfect, through the exalted wisdom endowed with a single instant. Relying on that, that learner becomes a non-learner, becoming manifestly perfectly a Buddha on the ground of great awakening, and by the power of having found the ultimate transformation of basis, thus, they "completely" "hold" a "completely" "pure" "buddhafield" that reaches the limits of space, without being partial or restricted, the naturally appearing realm of Akaniṣṭha, "and" as retinue, completely "pure" "sentient" "beings" as its contents, the great bodhisattvas of the tenth "ground". And, by attaining the body of exalted wisdom that has become equal to "all" "Buddhas", they completely hold the "continuum" of a Buddha, the nature of the three bodies demonstrating as a teacher in the ten directions of world systems for as long as infinite space exists, possessing a character that is without limits of direction "and" ends of time; "and" they "also" "completely" "hold" the "continuum" "of" the mode of "Dharma" of transmission and realization, which is without boundaries or limits; "likewise", the "continuum" of the noble "Sangha" practicing that Dharma of the Buddha in the world systems of the ten directions, which is without boundaries "and" limits, and they "completely" "hold" "all" "phenomena" of benefit and happiness belonging to existence and peace through great enlightened activity. They attain the ultimate result, the exalted wisdom body extending to the limits of the dharmadhatu, which has reached the culmination of abandonment and realization, is permanent, steadfast, and unchanging like space, and, like a wish-fulfilling jewel, performs benefit and happiness for as long as the boundaries and limits of samsara exist through spontaneously present great enlightened activity.

ཚུལ་ཁྲིམས༷་ཀྱིས༷་དུད༷་འགྲོ༷འི་འགྲོ༷་བ༷་རིགས་དང་གཟུགས་ལ་སོགས་པ་ཐ་དད་པ་སྣ་ཚོགས་སུ་གྱུར་པ་དུ༷་མའི༷་ངོ༷་བོ༷་དང༷་། དེར་མ་ཟད་མི༷་ཁོམས༷་པའི་གནས་བརྒྱ༷ད་ཆར་ཡང་སྤོང༷་བར་བྱེད་ཅིང་ཁྲིམས་དེ༷་ཡིས༷་དལ༷་བ༷་ཡིརྟེན་བཟང་པོ་རྟག༷་ཏུ༷་རྙེད༷་པར་བྱེད་དོ། །བཟོ༷ད་པས༷་ནི་གཟུགས༷་བཟང༷་བའི་དམ༷་པ༷་རྒྱ༷་ཆེན༷་པོ་མཚན་དཔེས་ལེགས་པར་བརྒྱན་པ་སངས་རྒྱས་ཀྱི་སྐུ་ཡི་བར་དུ་ཐོབ༷་པར་འགྱུར༷་ཏེ༷། གསེར༷་གྱི་མདོག་ལྟ་བུར་སྡུག༷་ཅིང༷་འགྲོ་བས༷་ལྟ༷་བར་བྱ་བའི༷་འོས༷་སུ༷་འགྱུར༷་རོ། །བརྩོན༷་འགྲུས༷་ཀྱིས༷་ནི༷་དཀར༷་པོའི༷་ཆོས་རྣམ༷ས་ཀྱི་ཡོན༷་ཏན༷་འགྲིབ༷་པར་མི༷་འགྱུར༷་བར་གོང་ནས་གོང་དུ་འཕེལ་བའི་མཐུས། ཡེ༷་ཤེས༷་མཐའ༷་ཡས༷་པ་རྒྱལ༷་བའི༷་ཡོན་ཏན་གྱི་བང༷་མཛོད༷་རྙེད༷་པར༷་འགྱུར༷་རོ། །བས༷མ་གཏན༷་གྱིས༷་ནི༷་འདོ༷ད་པའི༷་ཁམས་ཀྱི་འདོད་པའི་ཡོན༷་ཏན༷་ཉེས་དམིགས་ཆེ་ཞིང་བདེ་བ་ཆུང་བས་སྨད༷་པ༷་དག་གི་འོས་སུ་གྱུར་པ་འདོར༷་བར་བྱེད་ཅིང་། སྔོན་གནས་དང་ཟག་ཟད་དང་སེམས་ཤེས་ཏེ་རིག༷་པ་གསུམ་དང༷་། ལྷའི་རྣ་བ་དང་མིག་དང་རྫུ་འཕྲུལ་ཏེ་མངོ༷ན་པར༷་ཤེས༷་པ་གསུམ་སྟེ་སྔ་མ་དང༷་བསྡོམ་པས་དྲུག་པོ་དེ་དང་སེང་གེ་རྣམ་པར་བསྒྱིངས་པ་ལ་སོགས་པའི་ཏིང༷་ངེ་འཛིན༷་མངོ༷ན་པར༷་སྒྲུབ༷་པར་བྱེད་དོ། །ཤེས༷་རབ༷་ཀྱིས༷་ནི༷་ཆོས༷་ཐམས་ཅད་ཀྱི༷་རང༷་བཞིན༷་སྟོང་པ་ཉིད་ཡོངས༷་སུ་ཤེས༷་ནས༷་དངོས་པོར་འཛིན་པ་སྤངས་ཏེ་ཁ༷མས་གསུམ༷་མ༷་ལུས༷་པ༷་ལ༷ས་ཡང༷་དག༷་པར་འདའ༷་བར༷་འགྱུར༷་ལ། སྐུ་གཉིས་དང་ལྡན་པ་མི༷་ཡི༷་ཁྱུ༷་མཆོག༷་ཆོས་ཀྱི་རྒྱལ་པོ་སངས་རྒྱས་སུ་གྱུར་ཏེ་འཇིག་རྟེན་གྱི་ཁམས་ཀུན་ཏུ་མངའ་དབང་བསྒྱུར་བའི་ཕྲིན་ལས་ཀྱི་འཁོར༷་ལོ༷་རིན༷་པོ་ཆེ༷་རྒྱུན་མི་འཆད་པར་བསྐོར༷་བར་བྱས༷་ནས༷་སྡུག༷་བསྔལ༷་མཐའ་དག་གཏན་དུ་ཟ༷ད་པར༷་བྱ༷་བའི་ཕྱིར༷་འགྲོ༷་བ་རྣམས་ལ༷་དམ་པའི་ཆོས༷་ཀྱི་སྣང་བ་མཆོག་ཀྱང༷་སྟོན༷་པར་འགྱུར་རོ། །༈ལམ་ཡོངས་སུ་རྫོགས་པའི་འབྲས་བུ།

Second, one verse starting with "Having completely perfected this Dharma": Whoever abides in the Mahayana family, starting from when they first generate the mind of awakening, they practice "this" "Dharma" of the Mahayana path, the six perfections as explained, without exception, for three countless eons and so forth in a manner of skillful means. What is skillful means in that? It is rolling all those perfections into a single meaning without separating them, such that they mutually act as friends to one another, and practicing all of them perfectly within each one, and also practicing them in a manner where all of them become the essence of the perfection of wisdom endowed with all supreme aspects. By practicing in that way, "having" "completely" "perfected" the practice of all perfections to the utmost limit, that "bodhisattva" attains the great exalted wisdom at the end of the continuum of the tenth ground, which is able to actualize the dharmadhatu endowed with all supreme aspects, in which all undefiled phenomena are completely perfect, through the exalted wisdom endowed with a single instant. Relying on that, that learner becomes a non-learner, becoming manifestly perfectly a Buddha on the ground of great awakening, and by the power of having found the ultimate transformation of basis, thus, they "completely" "hold" a "completely" "pure" "buddhafield" that reaches the limits of space, without being partial or restricted, the naturally appearing realm of Akaniṣṭha, "and" as retinue, completely "pure" "sentient" "beings" as its contents, the great bodhisattvas of the tenth "ground". And, by attaining the body of exalted wisdom that has become equal to "all" "Buddhas", they completely hold the "continuum" of a Buddha, the nature of the three bodies demonstrating as a teacher in the ten directions of world systems for as long as infinite space exists, possessing a character that is without limits of direction "and" ends of time; "and" they "also" "completely" "hold" the "continuum" "of" the mode of "Dharma" of transmission and realization, which is without boundaries or limits; "likewise", the "continuum" of the noble "Sangha" practicing that Dharma of the Buddha in the world systems of the ten directions, which is without boundaries "and" limits, and they "completely" "hold" "all" "phenomena" of benefit and happiness belonging to existence and peace through great enlightened activity. They attain the ultimate result, the exalted wisdom body extending to the limits of the dharmadhatu, which has reached the culmination of abandonment and realization, is permanent, steadfast, and unchanging like space, and, like a wish-fulfilling jewel, performs benefit and happiness for as long as the boundaries and limits of samsara exist through spontaneously present great enlightened activity.

ཚུལ་ཁྲིམས༷་ཀྱིས༷་དུད༷་འགྲོ༷འི་འགྲོ༷་བ༷་རིགས་དང་གཟུགས་ལ་སོགས་པ་ཐ་དད་པ་སྣ་ཚོགས་སུ་གྱུར་པ་དུ༷་མའི༷་ངོ༷་བོ༷་དང༷་། དེར་མ་ཟད་མི༷་ཁོམས༷་པའི་གནས་བརྒྱ༷ད་ཆར་ཡང་སྤོང༷་བར་བྱེད་ཅིང་ཁྲིམས་དེ༷་ཡིས༷་དལ༷་བ༷་ཡིརྟེན་བཟང་པོ་རྟག༷་ཏུ༷་རྙེད༷་པར་བྱེད་དོ། །བཟོ༷ད་པས༷་ནི་གཟུགས༷་བཟང༷་བའི་དམ༷་པ༷་རྒྱ༷་ཆེན༷་པོ་མཚན་དཔེས་ལེགས་པར་བརྒྱན་པ་སངས་རྒྱས་ཀྱི་སྐུ་ཡི་བར་དུ་ཐོབ༷་པར་འགྱུར༷་ཏེ༷། གསེར༷་གྱི་མདོག་ལྟ་བུར་སྡུག༷་ཅིང༷་འགྲོ་བས༷་ལྟ༷་བར་བྱ་བའི༷་འོས༷་སུ༷་འགྱུར༷་རོ། །བརྩོན༷་འགྲུས༷་ཀྱིས༷་ནི༷་དཀར༷་པོའི༷་ཆོས་རྣམ༷ས་ཀྱི་ཡོན༷་ཏན༷་འགྲིབ༷་པར་མི༷་འགྱུར༷་བར་གོང་ནས་གོང་དུ་འཕེལ་བའི་མཐུས། ཡེ༷་ཤེས༷་མཐའ༷་ཡས༷་པ་རྒྱལ༷་བའི༷་ཡོན་ཏན་གྱི་བང༷་མཛོད༷་རྙེད༷་པར༷་འགྱུར༷་རོ། །བས༷མ་གཏན༷་གྱིས༷་ནི༷་འདོ༷ད་པའི༷་ཁམས་ཀྱི་འདོད་པའི་ཡོན༷་ཏན༷་ཉེས་དམིགས་ཆེ་ཞིང་བདེ་བ་ཆུང་བས་སྨད༷་པ༷་དག་གི་འོས་སུ་གྱུར་པ་འདོར༷་བར་བྱེད་ཅིང་། སྔོན་གནས་དང་ཟག་ཟད་དང་སེམས་ཤེས་ཏེ་རིག༷་པ་གསུམ་དང༷་། ལྷའི་རྣ་བ་དང་མིག་དང་རྫུ་འཕྲུལ་ཏེ་མངོ༷ན་པར༷་ཤེས༷་པ་གསུམ་སྟེ་སྔ་མ་དང༷་བསྡོམ་པས་དྲུག་པོ་དེ་དང་སེང་གེ་རྣམ་པར་བསྒྱིངས་པ་ལ་སོགས་པའི་ཏིང༷་ངེ་འཛིན༷་མངོ༷ན་པར༷་སྒྲུབ༷་པར་བྱེད་དོ། །ཤེས༷་རབ༷་ཀྱིས༷་ནི༷་ཆོས༷་ཐམས་ཅད་ཀྱི༷་རང༷་བཞིན༷་སྟོང་པ་ཉིད་ཡོངས༷་སུ་ཤེས༷་ནས༷་དངོས་པོར་འཛིན་པ་སྤངས་ཏེ་ཁ༷མས་གསུམ༷་མ༷་ལུས༷་པ༷་ལ༷ས་ཡང༷་དག༷་པར་འདའ༷་བར༷་འགྱུར༷་ལ། སྐུ་གཉིས་དང་ལྡན་པ་མི༷་ཡི༷་ཁྱུ༷་མཆོག༷་ཆོས་ཀྱི་རྒྱལ་པོ་སངས་རྒྱས་སུ་གྱུར་ཏེ་འཇིག་རྟེན་གྱི་ཁམས་ཀུན་ཏུ་མངའ་དབང་བསྒྱུར་བའི་ཕྲིན་ལས་ཀྱི་འཁོར༷་ལོ༷་རིན༷་པོ་ཆེ༷་རྒྱུན་མི་འཆད་པར་བསྐོར༷་བར་བྱས༷་ནས༷་སྡུག༷་བསྔལ༷་མཐའ་དག་གཏན་དུ་ཟ༷ད་པར༷་བྱ༷་བའི་ཕྱིར༷་འགྲོ༷་བ་རྣམས་ལ༷་དམ་པའི་ཆོས༷་ཀྱི་སྣང་བ་མཆོག་ཀྱང༷་སྟོན༷་པར་འགྱུར་རོ། །༈ལམ་ཡོངས་སུ་རྫོགས་པའི་འབྲས་བུ།

Second, one verse starting with "Having completely perfected this Dharma": Whoever abides in the Mahayana family, starting from when they first generate the mind of awakening, they practice "this" "Dharma" of the Mahayana path, the six perfections as explained, without exception, for three countless eons and so forth in a manner of skillful means. What is skillful means in that? It is rolling all those perfections into a single meaning without separating them, such that they mutually act as friends to one another, and practicing all of them perfectly within each one, and also practicing them in a manner where all of them become the essence of the perfection of wisdom endowed with all supreme aspects. By practicing in that way, "having" "completely" "perfected" the practice of all perfections to the utmost limit, that "bodhisattva" attains the great exalted wisdom at the end of the continuum of the tenth ground, which is able to actualize the dharmadhatu endowed with all supreme aspects, in which all undefiled phenomena are completely perfect, through the exalted wisdom endowed with a single instant. Relying on that, that learner becomes a non-learner, becoming manifestly perfectly a Buddha on the ground of great awakening, and by the power of having found the ultimate transformation of basis, thus, they "completely" "hold" a "completely" "pure" "buddhafield" that reaches the limits of space, without being partial or restricted, the naturally appearing realm of Akaniṣṭha, "and" as retinue, completely "pure" "sentient" "beings" as its contents, the great bodhisattvas of the tenth "ground". And, by attaining the body of exalted wisdom that has become equal to "all" "Buddhas", they completely hold the "continuum" of a Buddha, the nature of the three bodies demonstrating as a teacher in the ten directions of world systems for as long as infinite space exists, possessing a character that is without limits of direction "and" ends of time; "and" they "also" "completely" "hold" the "continuum" "of" the mode of "Dharma" of transmission and realization, which is without boundaries or limits; "likewise", the "continuum" of the noble "Sangha" practicing that Dharma of the Buddha in the world systems of the ten directions, which is without boundaries "and" limits, and they "completely" "hold" "all" "phenomena" of benefit and happiness belonging to existence and peace through great enlightened activity. They attain the ultimate result, the exalted wisdom body extending to the limits of the dharmadhatu, which has reached the culmination of abandonment and realization, is permanent, steadfast, and unchanging like space, and, like a wish-fulfilling jewel, performs benefit and happiness for as long as the boundaries and limits of samsara exist through spontaneously present great enlightened activity.

translation: Here it is said: The jewel of the *Precious Summary of Qualities* is the priceless, precious inner essence of the perfection of wisdom, which is the heart of the great ocean of the well-spoken words of the Buddha. Such a method of Dharma, which abides in the profound and peaceful space of the mind of the form body with supreme marks like a full moon, and which was well drawn forth from his glorious throat, is rare in all the worlds. I vividly recall the final testament before passing into peace left by the supreme speaker of truth, saying it is more regrettable if even a mere fraction of a word of the perfection of wisdom degenerates than if all other textual traditions of Dharma were to degenerate. My joy in explaining, listening to, and composing upon this text explicitly taught by the Sugata, whose exalted wisdom cannot be illustrated even in the slightest by tenth-ground bodhisattvas as numerous as the sands of the Ganges, increases immensely. Look, children of noble family! This Dharma is the treasury of vast Dharma, the ultimate of the profound; rejoice that it is the sacred congruent cause of the exalted wisdom of the Buddhas who have completely perfected the two accumulations. The stages of clear realization for practice are also immensely clarified by the meaning, and I have composed this flawless good tradition of explaining the intent of the explicit teaching by means of scripture, pith instruction, and reasoning. Through the virtue of this, in all my lifetimes, having well realized the profound meaning of the union of emptiness and dependent origination, may I never turn away from the good path that pleases the Buddhas. From now until attaining Buddhahood, may my wisdom increase in lifetime after lifetime, and may I act for the welfare of beings with great compassion that abandons mental engagement in one's own welfare, and with supreme skillful means. With a mind seeking to repay the kindness of the supreme Buddhas, holding the treasury of the Buddha's Dharma without exception, like the bodhisattvas Samantabhadra and Mañjughoṣa, may I propagate the enlightened activities of the Buddhas to the ends of existence. May all those who see, hear, reflect on, and so forth this text, and all who are connected to me through good or bad karma, swiftly clear away the thick darkness of views and abide on the irreversible ground. By the truth that this Dharma is well-spoken in accordance with the nature of phenomena, may all the Buddhas and their heirs generate the glory of intelligent eloquence in those who uphold this, so that they may be completely victorious in all directions. May all demonic samaya-breakers, barbarians, and so forth who harm the teachings, and the human and non-human dark forces, have their harmful thoughts and actions completely pacified even in the directions where the volumes of this text reside. By its blessings, may whatever dark illusions are fabricated as Dharma be destroyed without trace, and by the power of the blazing light of authentic Dharma, may the benefit and happiness of beings increase higher and higher. Even in this darkness where the dregs of time flourish, may the lunar phase of exceptional resolve increase, and may many beautiful things rise satisfyingly, radiating the light of ten million cooling rays of altruism. May the supreme upholders of the teachings live long, may the wealth of the patrons of the teachings also increase, and may all beings have faith in the essence of the teachings, so that the precious teachings may expand supremely. May I alone well establish the ocean of sentient beings pervading to the limits of space upon the good path of the perfection of wisdom, and may they all become perfect Buddhas. In whatever regions this text flourishes, may illnesses, poverty, and conflicts be pacified, may goals be accomplished in accordance with the Dharma, and may the festival of auspiciousness increase higher and higher. Thus, this explanation for entering without error into the intent of the Mother of the Conquerors, having as its substantial cause my own wish to compose it in order to place good imprints of the profound Dharma upon my own mind and so forth, due to my having had extraordinary devotion to this Dharma since I was young, and having as its cooperative conditions the great seeker, the yogi of the Early Translation Great Perfection, Rigdzin Natsok Rangdrol, repeatedly encouraging me with his words, and also the great follower of the Early Translation tradition, the sacred guru Lungtok, earnestly encouraging me, and being encouraged by many propounders of Dharma such as the widely heard one named Do Ngak—relying on this, I, Mipham Jampal Gyepai Dorje, whose conviction in this Dharma method became firm, relying on the eloquent explanations of the Indian and Tibetan commentaries, began it on the fourteenth day of the sixth lunar month in my forty-seventh year, the Water Dragon year of Joy, at the glorious upper cave known as Karmo Taktsang, a place blessed by the Lord of Conquerors Padma, in the place called Tashi Palbar Pema Deden Ling, and wrote as much as I could on consecutive days, adapting to when I had leisure. I completed it entirely on the twenty-eighth day of that month, an excellent time endowed with the Pushya constellation, with perfect auspicious conditions. By this, may wonderful benefits spread throughout all directions and times, unceasingly bringing benefit to the teachings and to all impartial sentient beings! Sarva maṅgalaṃ!
